cert_fields_required.text: Name, certificate, and private key are required

cert_pem_invalid.text: This is not a readable certificate. Paste the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- blocks, the server certificate first.

database_already_attached.text: That database is already attached to this app

database_in_use.text: Database '{$name}' is attached to {$workloads}; detach it on the app's Databases tab first

database_instance_server_mismatch.text: Database '{$name}' runs on {$server} while the app runs on {$instance_server}; a link network only exists on the daemon both share

database_name_taken.text: A database named '{$name}' already exists; destroy it first or pick another name

database_not_ready.text: Database '{$name}' is not ready yet (state: {$state}); the app would start without its credentials, so wait until it is active and deploy then

database_remote.text: Database '{$name}' runs on host '{$server}': its port is only published on that host's loopback, so sites on this host cannot reach it

database_server_mismatch.text: Database '{$name}' runs on host '{$server}' while this site deploys on host '{$site_server}': a Docker site reaches its database over a link network, which only exists when both run on the same host

domain_site_mismatch.text: The domain in the body names another site than the one in the URL

hostname_taken.text: That hostname is already configured for this site

route_taken.text: That hostname and path are already routed on this site

key_pem_invalid.text: This is not a readable private key. Paste the -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- block that belongs to the certificate.

local_server_immutable.text: The implicit local host cannot be edited

local_server_undeletable.text: The implicit local host cannot be removed

name_format.text: Use only lowercase letters, digits, and dashes

prefix_format.text: The env prefix must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits, and underscores

prefix_taken.text: Env prefix '{$prefix}' is already used by another database on this site

reserved_env_var.text: '{$name}' is a reserved control variable Hohenheim generates per process; it cannot be configured

tls_passthrough_backend_certificate.text: The backend presents the certificate for a TLS passthrough domain; do not assign a Hohenheim certificate

tls_passthrough_no_access_list.text: HTTP access lists cannot inspect encrypted TLS passthrough traffic

tls_passthrough_no_http_auth.text: HTTP authentication providers cannot inspect encrypted TLS passthrough traffic

tls_passthrough_no_http_options.text: HTTP headers, HSTS, and path stripping do not apply to untouched TLS streams

tls_passthrough_no_path.text: TLS passthrough routes by SNI hostname and cannot inspect URL paths

ssh_target_format.text: SSH target must be a plain [user@]host[:port]

url_scheme.text: The URL must start with http:// or https://

weak_api_key.text: This API key is too easy to guess: it would be recoverable from a database copy. Use the generate action, or paste a random key of at least {$min_length} characters

api_keys.text: Keys accepted by the managed process API. Only a digest is stored, so a key is never shown again: leave this empty to keep the stored keys, add a row to adopt a key you already hold, or use the row action to generate one.

auto_deploy.text: Deploy each new commit on this branch, whether the repository's push webhook reports it or the scheduled check finds it.

autoindex.text: Show a directory listing when no index file exists.

basic_auth_user.text: What the visitor types to get in.

basic_auth_password.text: Stored as a hash; nobody can read it back. When you edit a rule, leave it empty to keep the current password.

auth_provider_name.text: A recognizable name used when assigning this provider to a site.

auth_provider_type.text: The authentication method this provider uses.

auth_provider_config.text: Settings required by the selected provider type.

required_permission.text: A single permission name, e.g. "site.internal", checked against the identity's permission claims. Only used by claims-based providers such as Proteus (HTTP Basic Auth ignores it). Leave blank to demand hohenheim.site.<slug>, the permission named after the protected site.

credentials.text: One Basic Auth username and password per row. Passwords are stored hashed and never shown: leave a password blank to keep it, type one to replace it.

proteus_endpoint.text: Base URL of the Proteus identity service.

proteus_realm_client.text: Client identifier registered in the Proteus realm.

proteus_access_key.text: Secret access key used to call the Proteus realm.

proteus_authenticator.text: Slug of one specific Proteus sign-in method to force. Leave blank to let visitors choose from all sign-in methods the realm has enabled.

branch.text: Git branch to check out. Leave blank to use the repository default.

build_command.text: Shell command run after checkout and before a deployment becomes active.

build_directory.text: Working directory for the build command, relative to the repository root.

build_environment_variables.text: Environment variables available only while building the repository.

build_timeout.text: Maximum build duration in seconds before the deployment is cancelled; the host's build time quota still applies.

container_command.text: Optional command that overrides the image's default command.

container_port.text: TCP port on which the application listens inside the container.

connect_timeout.text: Maximum seconds allowed to establish the TCP connection to the passthrough backend.

cpu_limit.text: Maximum CPU cores available to the app. Leave blank for no limit.

delay.text: Artificial delay in milliseconds before handling each request.

dockerfile.text: Path to the Dockerfile, relative to the repository root.

builder.text: How a git checkout becomes an image. Nixpacks detects the language and needs no Dockerfile in the repository.

build_arguments.text: Values passed to the Dockerfile at BUILD time only. The runtime environment variables are deliberately not available to the build, so a build log can never leak them; a build argument does end up in the image history, so never put a secret here.

environment_variables.text: Variables passed to each application process at runtime.

fallback_file.text: File served when the requested path does not exist, for example index.html for an SPA.

not_found_page.text: The page visitors see, with a 404 status, when the address names no file. Left empty, a 404.html in the served folder is used when there is one.

forward_host.text: Hostname or IP address of the HTTP upstream.

forward_port.text: TCP port of the upstream. Defaults to 80 for HTTP and 443 for HTTPS.

more_backends.text: Further host:port addresses serving the same app, one per line. Requests take turns among all of them, skip one that stops answering and try the next when a connection is refused.

forward_scheme.text: http or https: how Hohenheim connects to where requests go.

proxy_protocol_v2.text: Send the binary PROXY v2 header before anything else on each connection, so the upstream learns the original client address and port and the address it connected to. The upstream must be set to expect the header: one that is not reads it as garbage and drops the connection. Off, the upstream sees this proxy as the client.

tls_forward_host.text: Hostname or IP address that receives the original, still-encrypted TLS stream.

tls_forward_port.text: TCP port that receives the original TLS stream.

ignore_certificates.text: Accept an invalid or self-signed certificate from the upstream.

docker_container_image.text: The image the container runs, as a registry names it (nginx, ghcr.io/team/app); it is pulled, never built.

docker_container_image_tag.text: The tag of the image to pull (alpine, 1.4).

image.text: Image name to run when no Dockerfile build is used.

image_tag.text: Tag applied to a locally built image.

indexes.text: Serve conventional index files such as index.html from directories.

maximum_processes.text: Upper scaling limit for concurrently running application processes.

memory_limit.text: Memory it may grow to; past it the kernel kills it. Leave blank for the default of its kind.

memory_reserved.text: Memory its host books for it; it may use more, up to its maximum. A change is booked at once, restarts nothing, and reaches a running Docker app at its next deploy or restart. Leave blank to reserve its maximum.

minimum_processes.text: Number of warm application processes Hohenheim keeps running.

node_runtime.text: Discovered Node.js version used to start this app.

poll_interval.text: Seconds between two checks of the repository for new commits while automatic deploys are on, at least 60. 0 never checks; a webhook still deploys on push.

port_argument.text: Command-line argument placed before the allocated port number.

preserve_path.text: Append the original request path and query string to the redirect target.

redirect_status.text: HTTP status code returned for the redirect.

repository_url.text: Git clone URL of a repository anyone may read. For a private repository, choose a Git connection below instead.

request_timeout.text: Maximum request lifetime in seconds, from 0 to {$max}. 0 removes the limit for streaming, gRPC and WebSocket backends.

idle_timeout.text: Ends a request when no byte moved in either direction for this many seconds, from 0 to {$max}. Empty or 0 sets no idle limit. The request timeout still limits the whole request: set that to 0 for long uploads and streams. Not applied once a connection is upgraded (WebSocket).

rewrite_location.text: Rewrite upstream redirects so they keep using the public site hostname.

upstream_protocol.text: HTTP/2 is required for gRPC backends. Cleartext upstreams then use prior-knowledge h2c.

root_path.text: Directory containing the files to serve; a relative path resolves against the Hohenheim working directory.

run_as_user.text: System account used for the child process, including its uid, gid and home directory.

script.text: Application entry script, relative to the working directory.

server.text: Host on which the container will run.

shallow_clone.text: Fetch only the latest history to reduce checkout time and disk use.

show_hidden_files.text: Allow files whose names start with a dot to be served or listed.

source.text: Use files already on this server or deploy them from a Git repository.

start_command.text: Executable and arguments used to start each application process.

submodules.text: Initialize and update repository submodules after checkout.

target_url.text: Absolute URL or root-relative path to which requests are redirected.

upstream_socket.text: Unix socket path. When set, it takes precedence over host and port.

use_ports.text: Allocate a loopback TCP port instead of the default Unix socket transport.

volumes.text: Container bind mounts in host-path:container-path form.

wait_for_ready.text: Route traffic only after the child reports that startup completed.

webhook_secret.text: Secret used to verify signed repository webhook requests.

websocket_upgrade.text: Forward WebSocket upgrade requests to the upstream.

working_directory.text: Directory in which the application command is started.

restarted_unanswered.text: {$subject} stopped answering its site and was restarted

auto_deploy_disabled.text: Auto-deploy is disabled: pushes are acknowledged but not deployed. Enable it in the application's source settings.

certificate.text: TLS certificate served for this hostname. Blank lets the platform pick or request one.

site_refusing.text: {$name} does not answer as it is set up

unknown_kind.text: Its upstream kind {$detail} is not known to this build, so none of its hostnames route

handler_failed.text: Its request handler could not be built, so none of its hostnames route: {$detail}

duplicate_route.text: One of its routes is already claimed by another site and is ignored: {$detail}

auth_unavailable.text: Its authentication provider cannot be built, so every request is refused: {$detail}

access_rule_unusable.text: An access rule cannot be evaluated and refuses every request it decides: {$detail}

spamservice_not_ready.text: The managed spam service is enabled but reports state "{$state}"

proteus_sign_in_held_back.text: Proteus sign-in is switched on without a required permission, so it is not offered: it would let in everyone the Proteus realm knows. Name the Proteus permission a person must hold, then restart Hohenheim.

listener_port_privileged.text: Port {$port} needs privileges this process does not have. Give Hohenheim's service the CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE capability, or set {$setting} to a port of 1024 or higher.

listener_port_in_use.text: Port {$port} is already used by another program. Stop that program, or set {$setting} to a free port.

stream_port_in_use.text: Port {$port}/{$protocol} of the stream {$name} is already held by {$holder}, so nothing is forwarded. Stop that program or move it to another port, or give the stream another public port on its page.

stream_port_privileged.text: Port {$port}/{$protocol} of the stream {$name} needs privileges this process does not have. Give Hohenheim's service the CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE capability, or give the stream a public port of 1024 or higher on its page.

stream_port_failed.text: Port {$port}/{$protocol} of the stream {$name} could not be opened: {$reason}. Give the stream another public port on its page if this keeps failing.

publish_description.text: Add every value below at your DNS provider. Values sharing a name must coexist; do not replace one with the other.

manual_ephemeral.text: This order remains available for 30 minutes and is lost when Hohenheim restarts. Manual DNS certificates do not auto-renew.

record_name.text: Owner name relative to the zone: @ for the zone itself, www for a subdomain, * for a wildcard

record_value.text: A/AAAA: an IP address. CNAME/NS/MX/SRV: a hostname. TXT: the text. CAA: flags tag value, e.g. 0 issue letsencrypt.org. TLSA: usage selector matching-type hex, e.g. 3 1 1 followed by the SHA-256 digest

domains_help.text: Add each hostname separately. Wildcards such as *.example.com require DNS-01 and do not cover the bare example.com name; include both when needed.

validation_help.text: HTTP-01 requires each exact hostname to route to this proxy. DNS-01 works for exact and wildcard names.

hook_ready.text: The configured hook publishes and removes TXT values, so this certificate can renew automatically.

hook_missing.text: Configure ssl.dns_hook_command in Settings to enable automatic DNS-01 issuance and renewal.

account_email_help.text: Overrides the global Let's Encrypt account email for this certificate.

proxy_unavailable.text: The proxy server is not available yet

dns_validation_failed.text: DNS validation failed. Verify every TXT value and start a new request.

domain_required.text: At least one domain is required

hostname_not_served.text: This installation does not serve {$hostnames}; add it as a domain first

hostname_not_managed.text: You do not manage the site serving {$hostnames}

reissue_requester_key.text: Its requester holds this certificate's key: only a new signing request from the requester re-orders it

signing_request_key_held_here.text: Hohenheim holds this certificate's key; a signing request cannot take it over

excluded_hostnames.text: Excluded from Let's Encrypt by their domain settings: {$hostnames}

hook_not_configured.text: The automated DNS hook is not configured in SSL / TLS settings

manual_expired.text: The manual DNS request expired or the server restarted. Start a new request.

renew_now_description.text: Asks Let's Encrypt for a new certificate for the same names now, as the nightly renewal would.

test_accepted.text: Test handed to the relay; it has not confirmed delivery

next_attempt_auto.text: None due yet; renewal is scheduled automatically before expiry

next_attempt_manual.text: Never; automatic renewal is switched off for this certificate

test_body.text: If you can read this, the channel works.

test_ok.text: Backup target {$name} is reachable and writable

clone_confirm.text: Create a copy with the same settings and domains (disabled by default)? API keys are not copied.

upstream_kind.text: What this site serves or forwards: static files, a redirect, an address, an app you manage, a TCP/UDP stream, ...

enabled.text: Disabled sites are not routed; requests get the offline page.

settings.text: This installation's settings, templates, images, git connections, engines, notification channels, backup targets and build.

access_list.text: Optional rule tree (addresses, passwords, sign-in) applied before requests reach the site.

auth_provider.text: Optional identity provider visitors must authenticate with before reaching the site.

listen_on.text: Only answer for this address on the selected local IP. Blank means all interfaces.

path_prefix.text: Only requests whose path starts with this prefix use this entry. Blank matches everything.

strip_path.text: Remove the matched path prefix before forwarding the request upstream.

force_ssl.text: Send visitors to HTTPS. Without a working certificate for this address they get an error page instead. A new address switches this on by itself once its certificate works.

hsts_enabled.text: Send the Strict-Transport-Security header so browsers refuse plain HTTP for this host.

custom_headers.text: Headers set on the request before it is forwarded upstream. An empty value removes the header.

response_headers.text: Headers set on the response sent to the client. An empty value removes the header.

exclude_from_letsencrypt.text: Leave this hostname out when requesting Let's Encrypt certificates for the site.

tls_passthrough_switch.text: This site passes TLS through to the app, so its HTTPS is handled there.

database_name.text: Unique name for this managed database; also names its container and volume. Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, starting with a letter or digit.

database_failure_reason.text: Why the last provision or destroy failed, as the host reported it. Cleared when the next attempt succeeds.

db_user.text: Username created in the database container and given to the apps it is attached to.

db_password.text: Password for the database user. Leave blank to generate one.

db_name.text: Name of the initial database created inside the engine.

ephemeral.text: Store data in a RAM-backed tmpfs: fast, but ALL data is lost when the container restarts.

records_hint.text: Open this zone's A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT and other DNS records.

origin.text: The name this zone answers for, e.g. example.com (no trailing dot)

soa_primary_ns.text: Hostname of the primary name server (the MNAME in the SOA record); leave empty for ns1.<zone>

soa_contact.text: Administrative contact for the zone; leave empty for hostmaster@<zone>

serial.text: The SOA serial. Hohenheim bumps it on every change; secondary servers compare it to decide whether to pull the zone again.

default_ttl.text: Seconds resolvers may cache records that set no explicit TTL (3600 = 1 hour)

negative_ttl.text: Seconds resolvers may cache name-does-not-exist answers (300 = 5 minutes)

soa_refresh.text: Seconds before a secondary name server re-checks this zone (7200 = 2 hours)

soa_retry.text: Seconds a secondary waits after a failed refresh before retrying (3600 = 1 hour)

soa_expire.text: Seconds after which a secondary that cannot reach this server stops answering (1209600 = 2 weeks)

zone_enabled.text: Disabled zones are not served and their names get REFUSED answers

record_zone.text: The authoritative zone this record belongs to.

record_type.text: The record type; MX and SRV also need a priority, SRV also needs a port

record_ttl.text: Seconds resolvers may cache this record; leave empty to use the zone default

record_priority.text: Required for MX and SRV records; lower numbers are tried first

record_weight.text: SRV only: relative weight for records with the same priority (0 when unsure)

record_port.text: SRV only: the TCP/UDP port the service listens on

record_enabled.text: Disabled records stay stored but are not served

ds_description.text: Lodge this DS record with your domain registrar to complete the DNSSEC chain of trust. It changes if you regenerate the signing key.

dnssec_enabled.text: Generate a signing key on first use and serve signed answers. Requires lodging the DS record (shown on the Zone file tab) with your registrar.

records_empty_description.text: Add A/AAAA records for your hosts and NS records for the zone itself.

records_unavailable.text: The DNS role is off on this node, so records cannot be listed here.

zone_file_description.text: The zone in standard master-file format; disabled rows appear as comments.

import_description.text: Paste standard zone-file text to load records into this zone.

import_replaces.text: Importing replaces every record of this zone except ACME-managed entries. SOA lines are ignored; the zone form owns those values.

delete_confirm.text: Detach database '{$database}' from app '{$instance}'? Reachability is revoked at the daemon as soon as you confirm, and the injected {$prefix} variables disappear at the app's next deploy. The database itself and its data are kept.
Delete this record on the owning peer?
Delete this peer? Its transfer key and admin credentials go with it, and the zones that notify it or accept transfers from it stop doing so. A peer a secondary zone still replicates from is refused.

Delete this sign-in provider? Its stored credentials and realm settings go with it. A provider still gating a site or named by an access rule is refused, because the proxy would fail those sites closed.
Delete this variable? It leaves its environment now; apps there stop receiving it at their next deploy, and anything running keeps the value it was deployed with until then.
Delete this access list? Its rules go with it, and every site and protected path it gates is let through unchecked from that moment on.
Delete this environment? An environment that still holds variables or apps is refused, so move or remove those first.
Delete this channel? The events it delivers stop being sent, with nothing left to report the gap.
Delete this host? Only its entry here is removed: the machine and everything running on it are untouched, and Hohenheim simply stops managing them.
Delete this stack? Its containers and network are destroyed; volumes are kept.
Delete this project? Its membership group and access grants are removed with it. A project still owning records or environments is refused.
Delete this ISO volume from the host? Apps no longer referencing it are unaffected.
Delete this rule? Anything nested inside it goes with it, and the change reaches live traffic immediately.
This removes the app from its host but keeps its data. Use "Delete with data" when the data must go too.
Delete this zone? Every record it holds goes with it and this server stops answering for the name.
Delete this site? Its hostnames stop answering and its preview deployments are destroyed. An app it points at is not deleted.
Delete this certificate? Its private key is destroyed and the names it covers stop serving HTTPS until another certificate covers them.
Delete '{$name}'? Its container and its data volume are destroyed, and the credentials are lost.
Delete engine '{$name}'? Its container and its data volume are destroyed. It is refused while any database still lives on it.

pre_deploy_command.text: Runs once before every deploy, in a temporary container made from the new version, with the app's variables and volumes. If it ends with an error or runs out of time, the deploy stops and the current version keeps serving. While it runs, Stop, Restart and Roll back of this app are refused. An app with an exclusive volume is stopped while the command runs. The command is ended at once when its time is up, and when Hohenheim itself restarts during it. Not run on a rollback, a restore, a preview or a restart. Split on spaces, no shell; \{\{KEY\}\} is not replaced, the variables are in the environment. Empty runs nothing. Containers that take their image from this app keep running the old version until the deploy switches.

image_from_app.text: Runs the image of the version this app serves, instead of an image of its own. After every deploy or rollback of the app this container is stopped and started again on that version, unless you stopped it yourself. Until the switch it keeps running the old version, also while a command before the deploy changes the database. A failed deploy leaves it on the old version; a rollback puts it on the older version and undoes no database change. Stopping the app does not stop this container. It is given {$seconds} seconds to stop. The app must be on the same host and have the same owner. Leave Container image and Image tag empty; the container keeps its own command, variables, limits and volumes.

Directory dumps are staged in before they go to the backup target; dumps written before the target existed stay here.
settings.hohenheim.database.backup_reten: Number of dumps kept per managed database on the backup target.
settings.hohenheim.database.backup_targe: Required backup target that receives every managed-database dump, encrypted; a filesystem target keeps them on this machine.
settings.hohenheim.database.control_plan: Required backup target that receives the control-plane recovery archives, which carry the master keys in the clear, so pick a target in another failure domain and protect it like the keyring file.
Upper bound for one managed-database dump; a dump that grows past it is cut off and its partial file deleted.
settings.hohenheim.database.path.label: Database file (retired)
settings.hohenheim.database.path.help: Retired: at the next start a value set here moves to zenit's database.url as the jdbc:sqlite: url of that file, a relative path resolved against the settings root; set database.url in settings/local.dry instead.
settings.hohenheim.database.url.label: Database URL (deprecated)
settings.hohenheim.database.url.help: Deprecated: SQLite JDBC URL used instead of the path when zenit's database.url is unset; any engine other than SQLite is refused at boot.
settings.hohenheim.dns.bind_address.help: Address the DNS listeners bind to.
settings.hohenheim.dns.enabled.label: DNS server
settings.hohenheim.dns.enabled.help: Serves the configured DNS zones authoritatively on UDP and TCP; the registrar must delegate each zone to this server, and production delegations need at least two name servers.
settings.hohenheim.dns.federation_name.h: Name this installation announces to a DNS peer when negotiating a shared transfer key, forming half of the TSIG key name; blank uses the system hostname.
settings.hohenheim.dns.nameservers.label: Nameservers
settings.hohenheim.dns.nameservers.help: Nameserver hostnames published for the zones this controller is primary for: a new primary zone gets one apex NS record per name, a zone-file import replaces the apex NS set with them, and the delegation check reports an apex NS set that disagrees.
settings.hohenheim.dns.port.label: DNS port
settings.hohenheim.dns.port.help: DNS listen port for UDP and TCP; port 53 usually needs elevated privileges or a capability such as CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE.
settings.hohenheim.dns.rate_limit_per_se: Responses per second allowed per client network and query over UDP against DNS reflection abuse, where every second limited response is sent truncated so clients retry over TCP; 0 disables it.
settings.hohenheim.files.max_entries.hel: Upper bound on the entries one directory listing returns; a larger directory refuses to list rather than show a truncated listing.
settings.hohenheim.files.max_file_kb.hel: Upper bound for one file read or written through the file manager, enforced during the transfer so a partial file never lands.
settings.hohenheim.sftp.enabled.label: SFTP for app files
settings.hohenheim.sftp.enabled.help: Run Hohenheim's own SFTP server: accounts sign in with an SFTP password or their SSH key and reach the same files, under the same rights, as the Files tab. Never the host's sshd or its accounts.
settings.hohenheim.sftp.port.label: SFTP port
settings.hohenheim.sftp.port.help: TCP port the SFTP server listens on; while SFTP is on it also joins the SSH ban rule, so an address banned for SSH brute force is dropped here too.
settings.hohenheim.sftp.bind_address.hel: Address the SFTP server binds to; blank listens on every address.
settings.hohenheim.sftp.public_host.help: The address the Files tab tells people to connect to; blank shows the address the admin page was opened on.
settings.hohenheim.sftp.max_file_mb.help: Largest file one SFTP read or upload moves; separate from the Files tab's limit because SFTP spools to disk.
settings.hohenheim.sftp.max_sessions.hel: Open SFTP sessions across all accounts; one more is refused when it signs in.
settings.hohenheim.sftp.max_sessions_per: Open SFTP sessions one account may hold at once.
settings.hohenheim.sftp.idle_timeout_min: Minutes without traffic after which an SFTP session is closed.
settings.hohenheim.networks.address_rang: Private IPv4 block from which every network Hohenheim creates for an app, a database link or a build takes its own small block, past every block the host's Docker networks and routes already use; networks that exist keep their addresses.
settings.hohenheim.networks.prefix_lengt: Prefix length of each network's block: /27 holds 29 containers besides the gateway, enough for an app's own containers, both ends of a link and the services of a stack.
settings.hohenheim.networks.free_warning: The dashboard warns about a host once fewer free networks than this are left in its address range; 0 never warns.
settings.hohenheim.hosts.contact_max_age: Minutes since a host's daemon last answered after which new apps are no longer placed on it, while apps already on it stay untouched; 0 or less removes the bound.
settings.hohenheim.incus.controller_pres: Hours another controller's presence stamp may go unrefreshed before its unreferenced shared objects count as abandoned; 0 or less disables reaping.
settings.hohenheim.incus.reap_departed_c: Removes the isolation ACL, extra-NIC bridge and presence marker of another controller whose presence stamp went unrefreshed past the grace period and whose objects nothing references; off makes every sweep report-only.
settings.hohenheim.instances.public_port: Size of the public port pre-allocation window; allocation fails loudly when every port in it is claimed or observed bound.
First host port of the pre-allocation window for public/UDP instance publications, which must be above 1024 and should stay clear of the kernel ephemeral range (32768-60999).
settings.hohenheim.logging.access_path.h: Path of the access log file.
settings.hohenheim.logging.access_to_fil: Writes proxied access requests to the access log file.
settings.hohenheim.logging.domain_misses: Path of the domain-miss log file; point a fail2ban jail's logpath here.
settings.hohenheim.logging.keep_days.hel: Days of the access log and the hostname-miss log kept: each log starts a new file every day and a day older than this is deleted; 0 keeps every day.
settings.hohenheim.logging.domain_misses: Writes a DOMAIN_MISS line for each address that keeps asking for names this server does not serve, so a fail2ban jail can ban it.
Hostname the generated preview hostnames live under, as site--ref.<this hostname>, covered by a wildcard certificate; previews refuse to deploy while it is unset.
settings.hohenheim.previews.lifetime_min: Minutes a preview lives before the expiry sweep reclaims it, extended by redeploying the same ref; values below 1 use the default.
settings.hohenheim.previews.max_per_owne: Concurrent live previews one owner may hold, enforced through the quota ledger; 0 or less means no cap.
settings.hohenheim.process.pids_limit.he: Maximum number of processes a host process Hohenheim runs as another system user (the managed spam service, a git command) may have under that user, so a fork bomb exhausts that user's budget instead of the host's process table; 0 or less uses the default.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.connection_prol: Maximum time a public connection may take to send what Hohenheim reads before routing it: an optional PROXY v2 header and, on the HTTPS port, the TLS ClientHello.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.force_https.hel: Sends visitors to HTTPS on every address with a working certificate.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.http_port.label: HTTP port
settings.hohenheim.proxy.http_port.help: Port the HTTP proxy listens on.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.http_socket_pat: Optional Unix socket the HTTP proxy listens on instead of a public TCP port; it bridges to a loopback port, counts every request as 127.0.0.1 unless a trusted fronting proxy forwards the client, and refuses to start until proxy.trusted_proxy_keys is set.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.http_socket_per: Octal permissions of the HTTP proxy Unix socket, which limit access to the socket only and not to its internal loopback port.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.https_port.help: Port the HTTPS proxy listens on.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.ipv6_address.he: Optional IPv6 address for dedicated proxy listeners.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.max_pending_con: Maximum connections per public listener that have not finished their prologue; excess connections are closed immediately.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.max_public_conn: Maximum simultaneous client connections each public listener accepts.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.not_found_messa: Error message for hostnames that match no site; leave it blank for the localized default, because a value here is shown to every visitor in every language.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.proxy_protocol_: IP addresses and CIDR ranges allowed to send a PROXY protocol v2 header on either public port; a non-empty list also moves the plain HTTP listener behind the shared ingress front, and an untrusted header is rejected.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.trusted_proxy_k: X-Hohenheim-Key values accepted from trusted upstream HTTP proxies.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.unreachable_mes: Error message for unreachable upstreams; leave it blank for the localized default, because a value here is shown to every visitor in every language.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.unknown_hosts.h: What the proxy answers for a hostname no site serves. Over HTTPS a name none of your certificates covers gets no certificate and its connection is closed, whatever you choose here.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.unknown_hosts_f: Address an unknown hostname is passed on to when Unknown hostnames is set to Forward to an address, for example http://localhost:8080.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.unknown_hosts_r: URL an unknown hostname is redirected to when Unknown hostnames is set to Redirect to a URL.
settings.hohenheim.proxy.unknown_hosts_s: Site that answers an unknown hostname when Unknown hostnames is set to One of your sites. It answers through one of its own addresses, so its access list and sign-in apply.

not_found_detail.text: Hohenheim's not-found page, with your not-found message when you set one.

forward_detail.text: Hohenheim passes the request on to the fallback address, for example a web server on this host.

redirect_detail.text: Visitors are sent on to one URL with a temporary redirect.

site_detail.text: A site you pick answers instead, with its own access list and sign-in.

drop_detail.text: The connection is closed without an answer, so scanners learn nothing.

settings.hohenheim.proxy_auth.persistent: Lifetime in seconds of a persistent proxy-auth (remember-me) cookie.
settings.hohenheim.proxy_auth.session_tt: Lifetime in seconds of a proxy-auth session.
settings.hohenheim.quota.max_databases_p: Default cap on the number of managed databases one owner may hold, charged on top of the engine container's app slot and overridden by a per-owner app quota; 0 or less means no cap.
settings.hohenheim.quota.max_disk_gb_per: Default cap on the total attached-disk size one owner may hold, summed over the devices of the owner's apps and overridden by a per-owner app quota; 0 or less means no cap.
settings.hohenheim.quota.max_extra_nics_: Default cap on the extra NICs, beyond the driver's primary one, that one owner may attach across apps, overridden by a per-owner app quota; 0 or less means no cap.
settings.hohenheim.quota.max_instances_p: Default maximum number of live apps one owner may hold, overridden by a per-owner app quota; 0 or less means no cap, and usage is counted either way.
settings.hohenheim.quota.max_memory_mb_p: Default cap on the total memory one owner's live apps may hold, each app charged its memory limit or its kind's declared footprint, overridden by a per-owner app quota; 0 or less means no cap.
settings.hohenheim.quota.max_sites_per_o: Default cap on the number of live sites one owner may hold, counted per site record and overridden by a per-owner app quota; 0 or less means no cap.
settings.hohenheim.releases.drain_second: How long the superseded release keeps running after traffic switched, so requests still pinned to it finish before it stops.
settings.hohenheim.releases.history_per_: Release operations kept per owning record; older ones are pruned when an operation completes.
settings.hohenheim.releases.probe_interv: Pause between health-probe attempts against the candidate's published loopback port.
settings.hohenheim.releases.probe_timeou: Time a candidate release has to give its first healthy HTTP response before it is destroyed while the prior release keeps serving.
settings.hohenheim.roles.databases.label: Databases role
settings.hohenheim.roles.databases.help: Runs managed databases: provisioning, backups and the site database links.
settings.hohenheim.roles.dns.label: DNS role
settings.hohenheim.roles.dns.help: Runs the DNS subsystem (zone store, federation and the authoritative server); the listener itself also requires dns.enabled.
settings.hohenheim.roles.firewall.label: Firewall role
settings.hohenheim.roles.firewall.help: Runs ban enforcement and spamservice reputation; nftables also requires security.nftables_enabled.
settings.hohenheim.roles.instances.label: Instances role
settings.hohenheim.roles.instances.help: Runs managed instances through the instance drivers and requires a reachable Docker daemon, which is probed at boot.
settings.hohenheim.roles.proxy.label: Proxy role
settings.hohenheim.roles.proxy.help: Runs the reverse proxy: public listeners, sites, domains, certificates and access lists.
settings.hohenheim.roles.stacks.label: Stacks role
settings.hohenheim.roles.stacks.help: Runs managed Docker stacks and requires a reachable Docker daemon, which is probed at boot.
settings.hohenheim.security.auto_ban_bud: Maximum automatic bans from any trigger within a sliding hour, after which further automatic bans are suppressed and logged; minimum 1, and manual bans are never limited.
settings.hohenheim.security.auto_ban_ttl: Lifetime of an automatically created ban.
settings.hohenheim.security.bans_enabled: Enforces IP bans in the proxy by refusing HTTP requests and TLS handshakes, and creates automatic bans when the event score crosses the threshold.
settings.hohenheim.security.container_lo: Number of rotated log files one managed container keeps, which times the rotation size caps its log disk use; 0 or less uses the default.
Size at which one managed container's log file rotates; 0 or less uses the default.
settings.hohenheim.security.container_pi: Maximum number of processes one managed container may run, so a fork bomb exhausts its own cgroup instead of the host's process table; 0 or less uses the default.
settings.hohenheim.security.default_even: Ban-score weight of event types that have no built-in weight.
settings.hohenheim.security.domain_miss_: Weighted event score within the window at which an IP is banned automatically.
Score forgiven for each successful route hit.
Hostname misses within the window before an IP's misses are recorded as security events.
Sliding window in which weighted security events count towards a ban.
settings.hohenheim.security.never_ban.he: IPs, CIDR ranges and hostnames that are never banned, automatically or manually; add your own operator addresses here. Hostnames resolve in the background and a resolved IPv6 address protects its whole /64.
settings.hohenheim.security.nftables_ena: Also enforces bans in the kernel via nftables, which requires passwordless sudo for nft and gives Hohenheim ownership of the table inet hohenheim.
settings.hohenheim.security.nftables_por: Comma-separated TCP ports the nftables ban rule applies to; never widen it to ports such as 22 or 53 that other services depend on.
settings.hohenheim.security.nftables_ssh: Comma-separated TCP ports of the second nftables ban rule, the one SSH brute-force bans land in, kept apart so an SSH attacker is not blocked from websites and a web scanner is not blocked from SSH.
settings.hohenheim.security.release_quar: Days a released hostname stays reserved for its former owner, refusing claims by a different owner to stop subdomain takeovers; 0 disables the quarantine.
settings.hohenheim.security.reputation_b: Comma-separated, case-insensitive spamservice event categories whose counts feed the reputation ban decision; dataset flags such as vpn, hosting, tor and proxy never count.
Weighted net spamservice event count across the configured categories at which an IP is banned; minimum 1.
settings.hohenheim.security.reputation_p: Number of negative events one positive event in the same category offsets; 0 disables positive credit.
settings.hohenheim.security.reputation_t: How long a spamservice reputation answer is cached in-process, at least 1 second.
settings.hohenheim.security.ssh_watch_en: Watches the local sshd journal for brute-force patterns and feeds them to the threat scorer that also bans hostname scanners, which requires the service user to be in the systemd-journal group.
settings.hohenheim.ssl.acme_directory_ur: ACME directory URL of the certificate authority; empty uses Let's Encrypt, production or staging per the staging switch.
Executable DNS-01 hook, called as: command present|cleanup record-name record-value.
settings.hohenheim.ssl.dns_propagation_s: Seconds to wait after publishing DNS-01 TXT records.
settings.hohenheim.ssl.letsencrypt_email: Email address of the Let's Encrypt account.
settings.hohenheim.ssl.letsencrypt_stagi: Uses the Let's Encrypt staging server instead of production.
settings.hohenheim.stacks.reclaim_images: Periodically removes superseded images of the repositories managed stacks declare, on every host that runs a stack, never touching an image referenced outside those repositories or by any container, and never touching volumes.
settings.hohenheim.stacks.reclaim_min_ag: Images whose build stamp is more recent than this many hours are kept, protecting freshly built images; minimum 1.
settings.hohenheim.stacks.reclaim_untrac: Also removes images with no tag or digest at all, which Hohenheim cannot prove are its own, like docker image prune does; keep it off on a shared host.
settings.hohenheim.storage.data_path.hel: Base directory for persistent data such as git repositories.
settings.hohenheim.storage.volume_root.h: Directory on the workload host that holds instance volumes; empty derives it from the data path, so set it when the controller and its hosts do not share a filesystem.
settings.hohenheim.storage.volume_uid_ba: First host uid workspaces are mapped to, each workspace running as this number plus its instance id, which must stay below the subuid range Incus gives unprivileged containers (1000000).

uses_production.text: This orders a real certificate from Let's Encrypt (production), which counts against its rate limits.

dns_mode_help.text: Where the TXT records Let's Encrypt checks are published. Manual: you add them at your DNS provider, then choose Verify DNS on the certificate.

mcp_publish_then_renew.text: The order waits for these TXT records: publish them (dns_record_set, in a zone this installation serves, or at your DNS provider), then call certificate_renew code={$code}.

verify_dns_hint.text: Checks the published TXT records and finishes the order.

letsencrypt_disabled.text: Let's Encrypt is switched off in Settings.

does_not_point_here.text: {$hostname} does not point here yet, it points to {$addresses}.

does_not_resolve.text: {$hostname} does not resolve yet. Point it at this server first.

acme_unauthorized.text: Let's Encrypt could not confirm that this server answers for these names. Check that each name points here.

acme_connection.text: Let's Encrypt could not reach this server over HTTP for one of the names. Check the firewall and that port 80 is open.

acme_dns.text: Let's Encrypt could not look up one of the names in DNS.

acme_rate_limited.text: Let's Encrypt refused because too many certificates were requested recently. Try again later.

acme_caa.text: A CAA record on the domain does not allow Let's Encrypt to issue for it.

acme_rejected_identifier.text: Let's Encrypt does not issue certificates for one of these names.

acme_other.text: Let's Encrypt did not issue the certificate. The certificate's renewal error and the server log have the details.

access_list_admits_everyone.text: {$list} lets every visitor through: none of its rules is switched on. Add a rule to it first, then pick it here.

access_list_would_open.text: This would leave {$list} letting every visitor through, and it protects {$path}. Keep at least one rule switched on, or remove the protection first.

host_check_failed.text: Host {$name} is not admitted yet. These checks must pass first: {$checks}. The host page lists what to do about each one.

open_protected_path.text: Its access list has no rule switched on, so it guards nothing. Add a rule to the list, or remove the protection.

check_and_admit_hint.text: Runs every check on this host. A host waiting for admission is admitted as soon as all required checks pass.

host_checked.text: Host {$name} checked: every required check passes

host_checked_failing.text: Host {$name} checked; these required checks fail: {$checks}

host_checked_admitted.text: Host {$name} passed every required check and is admitted

kind_needs_runtime_host.text: Needs a host running {$runtime}. Add one under Hosts first.

kind_needs_host.text: Needs a host. Add one under Hosts first.

fix_daemon.text: Start the container daemon on the host and make sure Hohenheim can reach its socket or endpoint.

fix_container_kernel.text: The probe container did not run. Make sure the daemon can pull and start images (disk space, registry access).

fix_cgroup_pids_controller.text: Boot the host with cgroup v2 and the pids controller enabled.

fix_pids_limit_enforced.text: The kernel did not enforce a container's process limit. Use cgroup v2 with the pids controller enabled.

fix_seccomp.text: Run containers with Docker's default seccomp profile; remove any unconfined default from the daemon configuration.

fix_no_new_privs.text: Set "no-new-privileges": true in /etc/docker/daemon.json and restart Docker.

fix_userns_remap.text: Set "userns-remap": "default" in /etc/docker/daemon.json and restart Docker, so root in a container is not root on the host.

fix_lsm.text: Enable AppArmor or SELinux on the host so containers run confined.

fix_network_headroom.text: Remove unused container networks, or widen hohenheim.networks.address_range.

fix_nftables.text: Install nftables on the host; Hohenheim manages its own table through its helper.

fix_resources.text: Give the Incus host more CPU or memory, or place apps on another host.

fix_trusted.text: Trust this controller's client certificate on the Incus host.

fix_driver_lxc.text: Install and enable the LXC driver for Incus on the host.

fix_storage_pool.text: Create the Incus storage pool this host is configured to use.

fix_managed_network.text: Create the Incus managed network this host is configured to use.

fix_network_acl.text: Use an Incus-managed bridge network, which supports network ACLs.

fix_lan_parent.text: Name an existing bridge or uplink of this host that Incus does not manage and that is up, or clear the local network interface.

fix_kernel_isolation_lane.text: This host gives containers no isolated kernel lane. Enable it, or run tenant apps in virtual machines.

fix_container_userns.text: Run Incus containers unprivileged, with a user namespace mapping.

fix_container_seccomp.text: Run Incus containers with seccomp filtering enabled.

published_ports.text: Ports published on every address of the host, by name: game, query, rcon or voice, then [host port:]container port/protocol, such as 25565/tcp. An empty host port is picked when it starts.

Ports published on every address of the host, by name: game, query, rcon or voice, then [host port:]port in the virtual machine/protocol, such as 25565/tcp. An empty host port is picked when it starts.

srv_service.text: The service a game address publishes an SRV record for, such as minecraft for _minecraft._tcp.

game_address.text: A name in a zone Hohenheim manages, such as mc.example.com: it points at this host and gets an SRV record for the game port. Empty: no game address, and its records go.

port_spec_invalid.text: Port {$name} is not written as [host port:]container port/protocol: {$spec}.

game_address_no_zone.text: No zone Hohenheim manages covers {$address}. Add the zone under DNS first, or leave the game address empty.

done_game_address.text: {$address} points here, with its SRV record

done_live.text: Its first start went out to its host

done_live_waiting.text: Not started yet: the app's page says what it waits for

step_address_where_lead.text: Its name, the address visitors use, and what Hohenheim's proxy answers there. Nothing runs on a host for it.

https_wildcard_help.text: One certificate for every name under the parent domain, proven through a DNS zone Hohenheim manages.

https_existing_help.text: Uses the certificate that already covers this address, a wildcard one included.

https_upload_help.text: Paste the certificate chain and its private key. The key is stored encrypted.

outcome_https_wildcard_apex.text: {$address} has no parent domain for a wildcard certificate to cover. Choose another option.

outcome_https_existing_none.text: No working certificate in Hohenheim covers {$address} yet. Choose another option.

cert_key_mismatch.text: This private key does not belong to the first certificate in the chain.

cert_chain_order.text: Certificate {$position} in the chain is not issued by certificate {$next}: put the server certificate first, then each issuer in order.

cert_expired.text: Certificate {$position} in the chain expired on {$date :datetime}.

cert_not_yet_valid.text: Certificate {$position} in the chain is not valid before {$date :datetime}.

static_site.text: A website from a git repository: built on its host, served as plain files

output_directory.text: The folder that is served, relative to the repository root. Leave it empty to serve the root itself.

build_image.text: The image the build command runs in. Leave it empty for Node.js 22.

static_site_owns_no_container.text: A static site never runs a container itself; each deploy generates a release that serves it

stream.text: Forward public ports of this proxy to ports of one address, unread: SSH, a database, a game server, a mail server

stream_ports.text: One row per port clients connect to on the host this proxy runs on, which no other app, stream or program may use: the public port, then the port at the address it forwards to with its protocol and, for a PROXY v2 header, proxy-v2 after it, such as 2525/tcp proxy-v2. A port alone forwards TCP.

stream_port_listen.text: The public port clients connect to; an entry naming a port the site already forwards replaces it.

stream_port_forward.text: The port at forward_host that receives what arrives on the public port.

stream_port_protocol.text: tcp, udp or both; tcp when left out.

stream_port_proxy.text: Set true to start each TCP connection with a PROXY v2 header carrying the client's address; the upstream must expect it.

stream_forward_host.text: The host name or IP address every public port forwards to: the host of an app's published port, a machine, or any address this proxy can reach.

stream_connect_timeout.text: Maximum seconds to open a TCP connection to the forwarded address.

stream_access_list.text: Optional: only its address rules apply to a stream, so clients from a denied network are dropped. A password or a sign-in cannot be asked on a raw port.

stream_enabled.text: Switched off, the stream forwards nothing; its ports stay reserved for it, so switching it on again restores forwarding.

stream_lead.text: Claims public ports on this proxy's host and forwards what arrives there, unread, to an address you give.

step_stream_where_lead.text: Its name and the address it forwards to. Nothing runs on a host for it.

step_stream_ports_lead.text: The public ports clients connect to, each with the port it forwards to. An access list applies by address only: a stream cannot ask for a password.

stream_no_http_auth.text: A TCP/UDP stream is forwarded unread, so it cannot send anyone to a login. Remove the login provider.

stream_access_list_credentials.text: This access list asks for a password or a login, which a TCP/UDP stream cannot do. Pick a list with address rules only.

stream_port_invalid.text: Port {$port} is not written as a port to forward to with its protocol, such as 2525/tcp, and proxy-v2 after it for a PROXY v2 header: {$spec}.

stream_port_proxy_protocol_tcp_only.text: Port {$port} forwards UDP, which never carries a PROXY v2 header. Forward it over TCP only, or leave proxy-v2 off.

stream_ports_required.text: A TCP/UDP stream forwards at least one public port.

stream_connect_hint.text: Clients connect to these ports of the proxy's host; each forwards what arrives, unread, to the address its row names.

variables_lead.text: Every app in this environment gets these values at its next deploy; an app's own value for the same key wins.

environments_lead.text: The environments this project deploys into, each with the variables its apps start with.

members_lead.text: Someone belongs to this project by holding its role: under Access, People, give them the role named after this project.

detach_confirm_any.text: Detach this database? The app can no longer reach it as soon as you confirm. The database itself and its data are kept.

none_attachable.text: Every database you may attach here is attached already.

databases_lead.text: This app's data in its databases is backed up with each database, not with the app.

backups_lead.text: A copy of this app's files, kept at its backup target. Restore one into a new app or over this one.

snapshots_lead.text: A quick copy kept on this host, to go back to before a risky change. It is lost with the host.

schedules_lead.text: Make backups or snapshots by themselves, for example every night.

no_target_body.text: Backups need a place to go. Until one is chosen, none can be made.

restore_needs_running.text: A dump can only be restored into a running database. Status now: {$state}.

spec_unchanged.text: Nothing else changes: both releases run the same settings.

rollback_step.text: Switch to the kept release, behind the health gate

status_probe.text: How Hohenheim asks this service for a small live figure, such as its players online, shown on its overview and in the list. It asks the published game port while somebody looks. Empty: no live figure.

build_hooks_lead.text: A build hook is a secret URL: anything that POSTs to it, a CMS publishing or a job elsewhere, deploys this app. It answers over HTTPS only, so a new URL shown as a bare path means no address of this app has a working certificate yet: add one, or prefix the path with an https address that has one.

build_hooks_empty.text: No build hooks yet. Create one to let a CMS or a scheduled job deploy this app.

build_hook_name_help.text: What will POST this URL, for example Headless CMS or Nightly rebuild.

build_hook_regenerate.text: {$actor} regenerated the URL of build hook {$subject}

build_hook_regenerate_confirm.text: The current URL stops working at once. Whatever POSTs it needs the new one, which is shown only once.

build_hook_regenerated.text: The new URL of this build hook, shown only now: {$url}

build_hook_revoke_confirm.text: Its URL stops working at once and cannot be restored. The releases it started keep naming it.

hook_does_not_start_stopped_workload.text: '{$name}' is not running, so the build hook did not deploy it: a build hook never starts an app someone stopped. Start it yourself first.

build_hook_name_invalid.text: Give the build hook a name of at most {$max} characters.

build_hook_needs_application.text: Only an app that deploys releases takes a build hook.

build_hook_already_revoked.text: This build hook is revoked; create a new one instead.

build_hook_revoked_before_start.text: The build hook that asked for this deploy was revoked before it started.

build_hook_regenerated_before_start.text: The URL of the build hook that asked for this deploy was regenerated before it started.

back_up_no_target.text: No backup target is set for database dumps; choose one in Settings, under Database.

back_up_target_missing.text: The backup target {$target} that database dumps go to does not exist.

backup_target_database_dumps.text: Backup target {$name} receives the managed-database dumps; pick another target for them in Settings, under Database, first

database_dump_kind_mismatch.text: This dump was taken from a database of another kind.

database_dump_kind_mismatch_detail.text: This dump was taken from a {$dump} database; it cannot be restored into a {$database} database.

database_dump_source_gone.text: The database this dump was taken from no longer exists; restore it into a new database instead.

database_restore_failed_unchanged_detail.text: The restore of {$name} failed and was rolled back: the database is as it was. {$reason}

database_restore_failed_mixed_detail.text: The restore of {$name} failed part way: the database may now hold a mix of the restored backup and its previous contents. Restore the backup taken just before it, from {$before :datetime} (#{$dump}), to bring the database back. {$reason}

database_restore_new_cleanup_failed_deta.text: The restore into the new database {$name} failed ({$reason}), and the half-restored database could not be removed ({$cleanup}); delete it before using the name again.

database_busy.text: A backup, restore or provisioning of this database is running; try again once it has finished.

database_dump_whole_server.text: A dump made with --create or pg_dumpall cannot be restored into one database.

database_dump_whole_server_detail.text: The dump for {$name} creates or connects to a database of its own ({$statement}): a dump made with --create, pg_dumpall or mysqldump --databases cannot be restored into one database. Dump the one database without those options; nothing was changed.

database_staging_unsafe.text: The dump staging directory cannot be restricted to its owner.

database_staging_unsafe_detail.text: The dump staging directory {$path} cannot be restricted to its owner ({$reason}); no dump or restore runs until it can, because a plaintext dump passes through it.

git_key_directory_not_private.text: The SSH key directory {$path} cannot be restricted to its owner (its filesystem refuses owner-only permissions, or something other than a directory of its own stands there), so no key is written into it. Move Hohenheim's data directory to a filesystem that keeps POSIX permissions, or make this directory its owner's alone (chmod 700).

host_identity_not_private.text: The private SSH key {$path} cannot be restricted to its owner (its filesystem refuses owner-only permissions, or a symbolic link stands there), so it is not written. Move Hohenheim's data directory to a filesystem that keeps POSIX permissions, or remove what stands at that path.

restore_upload_confirm.text: A fresh backup of {$name} is stored on the backup target first; then the uploaded dump is loaded into it, replacing the tables the dump holds.

restore_database_dump.text: {$actor} restored database backup {$subject} into a new database

dump_lead.text: Dumps of this database, stored encrypted on the backup target.

dump_new_name_help.text: The backup is restored into a new database of the same kind and version with this name; the source keeps running.

dump_restore_new_confirm.text: A new database is created from this backup; the database it was taken from is left as it is.

dump_restore_in_place_confirm_generic.text: A fresh backup of the database is taken first; then its contents are replaced with this backup.

dump_restore_in_place_confirm.text: A fresh backup of {$name} is taken first; then its contents are replaced with the backup from {$at}.

dump_restored_in_place.text: Restored {$name}; the backup taken just before is the one from {$before}

deploy_from_repository_description.text: Hohenheim builds the repository and serves it; this site keeps its addresses and protection; every push deploys.

repository_required.text: Name the repository to deploy: its URL, or a Git connection and one of its repositories.

done_switch.text: This site now serves the app

repository_outcome.text: This site now serves the app built from the repository. Every push deploys.

repository_outcome_folder.text: This site now serves the app built from the repository. It served the folder {$folder} before; that folder is still on disk.

repository_deployed.text: Deployed from a repository; it served the folder {$path} before

reaches_at_deploy.text: The app gets the change at its next deploy.

linked_server_note.text: What it is to this server

linked_server_join_code_help.text: Get the join code on that server under Servers, Let another Hohenheim manage this server. It is valid for 10 minutes.

linked_server_added.text: {$name} is added. This server manages it now.

linked_server_code_waiting.text: A join code is waiting, valid until {$until :datetime}. It was shown once; ask a new one if you lost it.

linked_server_not_managed.text: No other Hohenheim manages this server.

linked_server_removed_kept_there.text: {$name} is removed here. It did not answer, so it still holds the link until it is removed there.

linked_server_removed_not_sent.text: {$name} is removed here. Nothing was sent to its address: another server answers there.

linked_server_tool_not_answering.text: {$name} does not answer; nothing was changed.

linked_server_tool_may_have_arrived.text: {$name} did not answer in time. The change may or may not have been made there: read it again before you try again.

linked_server_tool_refused.text: {$name} does not take calls from this server now; nothing was changed.

linked_server_tool_gone.text: The server this is kept on is no longer linked to this server; nothing was changed.

linked_server_tool_no_shared_sign_in.text: Acting on {$name} from here needs a person who signs in with Proteus, here and on {$name}. Sign in here with Proteus once, then use a key of that account.

linked_server_tool_other_realm.text: {$name} does not sign people in with this server's Proteus realm, so nobody can act on it from here; nothing was changed.

linked_server_join_busy.text: Another link or change is under way there at this moment. Try again in a minute.

linked_server_join_unreadable.text: The other server's answer could not be read. Is it a Hohenheim that links servers?

linked_server_other_server.text: Another server answers at the address of {$name}

start_instance_description.text: Starts the stopped app the way a deploy starts it, without changing its settings or its data. Refused while a database the app uses is not ready.

stop_instance_description.text: Stops the app. Its data, volumes and ports are kept, so start brings it back; an app that is already stopped stays as it is.

restart_instance_description.text: Stops the app and starts it again with its current settings; its data is kept. An app whose releases Hohenheim manages starts again as a fresh deploy.

deploy_instance_description.text: Puts the app's newest version online, in the background. An app or static site is built, its pre-deploy command runs, the new version starts beside the old one, is checked over HTTP and takes over; a failed step leaves the old version serving. A workspace builds from its repository and restarts; other kinds start their app again.

drop_kept_release_description.text: Removes the earlier release an app keeps for roll back: its container, its network and the memory it holds on its host. Roll back then has nothing to go back to until the next deploy keeps one.

backup_instance_description.text: Backs the app's volumes up to its backup target now. The app is stopped while its data is copied and started again before the upload.

connect_push_webhook_description.text: Registers the push webhook at the git provider the app's source comes from, or brings it up to date, so a push starts a deploy. Stores a webhook secret when the app has none.

snapshot_instance_description.text: Takes a snapshot of the app's volumes on its host, which restore can put back later. The app is stopped while the copy is made and started again afterwards.

install_instance_description.text: Runs the install step of the app's template, or resumes or retries it, while that install is not done.

reinstall_instance_description.text: Runs the template's install step again as the template's data policy says: preserve runs it over the existing volumes; clear first removes the app and its volumes, which cannot be undone.

destroy_instance_data_description.text: Deletes the app and removes its volumes and their data from the host. This cannot be undone; delete keeps the data.

delete_instance_description.text: Deletes the app: its container is removed and its ports released. Its volumes and their data stay on the host, where the reconciler reports them; delete with data removes those too.

attach_install_media_description.text: Puts an ISO that is on the machine's host into the machine's drive, to boot an installer from. Only for a virtual machine with no ISO attached.

detach_install_media_description.text: Takes every ISO out of the machine's drives; the ISO files stay on the host.

console_command_instance_description.text: Sends one line to the app's main process, as if typed in its console. Nothing else changes.

app_update_instance_description.text: Runs the update script of the app's template inside the running app and answers its output. It changes no setting. Refused when the template has no update script or the app is not running.

delete_backup_description.text: Deletes the backup: its file is removed from the backup target, then its record. It cannot be restored afterwards.

restore_snapshot_description.text: Puts the snapshot back: every volume of the app is replaced by the snapshot's contents, so files written since the snapshot are lost.

delete_snapshot_description.text: Deletes the snapshot and its stored copy; the app is not touched.

detach_device_description.text: Removes this device from the app it is attached to; a disk's data is deleted with it and cannot be restored, the app's other data stays.

delete_instance_database_description.text: Removes the link between the app and the database; the database and its data are not touched.

create_instance_from_template_descriptio.text: Creates a new app from this template, with the name, project and values for the template's variables given. Only an administrator chooses its host.

approve_template_description.text: Approves the template after checking its install and update scripts, so apps can be made from it.

unapprove_template_description.text: Withdraws the template's approval. The template and the apps made from it stay.

destroy_volume_description.text: Removes the volume's directory and its data from the host, then its record. This cannot be undone; a workspace's home volume is refused.

expire_preview_description.text: Ends the preview deployment now: its app is removed, its generated address and DNS records go, and its checkout is deleted.

read_instance_log_description.text: Reads the newest lines the app printed.

list_instance_deploys_description.text: Lists the app's deploys and builds, newest first, a page at a time, each by its code, so their logs can be read.

read_build_log_description.text: Reads the stored log of one build.

read_deploy_log_description.text: Reads the stored log of one deploy.

list_instance_variables_description.text: Lists the app's environment variables. A plain one shows its value; a secret shows only that it is set.

set_instance_variable_description.text: Sets a plain environment variable of the app. The app sees it from its next deploy; nothing is restarted. A key that holds a secret is refused.

unset_instance_variable_description.text: Removes an environment variable of the app. The app stops seeing it from its next deploy; nothing is restarted.

set_instance_variables_description.text: Sets, replaces, generates and removes several variables of the app in one write, all or nothing. The app sees them from its next deploy; nothing is restarted. Answers the keys changed, never a value.

variables_set_help.text: Plain values to set; a key holding a secret is refused, so unset it first.

variables_secret_help.text: Variables to hold these values as secrets, replacing whatever the key held.

variables_generate_help.text: Keys Hohenheim fills with a random secret; a key that holds a value is refused.

variables_unset_help.text: Keys to remove, their values lost for good; a key the app holds nothing under is refused.

variables_none_given.text: Give at least one of set, secret, generate, unset.

app_create_needs_admin.text: Only an administrator creates an app without a template; create one from a template with app_create_from_template.

app_kind_other.text: {$code} is a {$kind} app; change it with {$tool}, or give change_kind: true to turn it into this kind.

app_kind_other_untooled.text: {$code} is a {$kind} app; give change_kind: true to turn it into this kind.

app_create_host.text: The host's code (SR1); left out, any host that runs this kind and has room is picked.

app_create_project.text: The project (PR3) whose members manage the new app; left out, the app is yours. It counts against the limits of the project's membership role.

app_backup_target.text: The backup target (BT1) the app's backups go to; an app without one cannot be backed up.

app_image_app.text: The Application (AP12), on the same host and of the same owner, whose serving image this container runs instead of image and tag; null clears it. A running container restarts on each new release of that app (deploy or roll_back); a stopped one takes it at its next start.

app_change_kind.text: Set true to turn the app of another kind named by code into this kind; without it such a code is refused. The new kind must be one the app's host runs, and a deployed app never switches between a virtual machine and another kind. Settings the new kind lacks are deleted for good.

create_application_app_description.text: Creates an Application from its settings through the panel's own create; nothing is deployed.

change_application_app_description.text: Changes the settings sent of an Application through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

create_docker_container_app_description.text: Creates a Docker container app from its settings through the panel's own create; nothing is started.

change_docker_container_app_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a Docker container app through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

create_static_site_app_description.text: Creates a Static site app from its settings through the panel's own create; nothing is deployed.

change_static_site_app_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a Static site app through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

mcp_tool_logs.text: Reads a log. An app's code (AP12): the newest lines it printed, every secret value of the app masked; this works on a stopped app too. A build's code (BU60): that build's whole stored log. A deploy's code (RL77): that deploy's whole step log, which names hosts and paths and so is for administrators only. app_deploy_list names them. The log is the app's own text, marked untrusted.

mcp_code_logs.text: Whose log to read: an app (AP12), a build (BU60) or a deploy (RL77). A code of any other kind is refused.

mcp_tool_delete.text: Deletes one record by its code; refused while the record is in use, with the reason. A delete cannot be undone, except a site (S20), which goes to the trash (site_restore brings it back; permanent removes a trashed one for good). Lost for good: a database (DB12) or engine (DE3) with its data, a volume (VO5) or disk device (DV3) with its data, a backup (BK30), snapshot (SN14) or dump (DD41) with its file. An app's volumes stay unless with_data; a host only leaves the panel; a person (U4) goes with every session, a role (RO2) only once it has no members, and one of your own API keys (AK3) is revoked. A notification channel (NC2) goes at once and its alerts stop silently. Answers what was removed.

mcp_code_delete.text: The record to delete, by the code the tools show for it.

mcp_with_data.text: Also removes the app's volumes and their data from the host, which cannot be undone; without it the host check lists them as leftovers.

mcp_force.text: Removes the record without verifying its container and volume are gone, for an unreachable host. The host check lists what survives as leftovers.

mcp_permanent.text: Removes a site that is in the trash for good; without it a site is moved to the trash.

mcp_drop.text: Removes the release an app keeps for roll back instead of going back to it: its container, network and memory go. Apps only.

mcp_tool_site_restore.text: Brings a site back. One in the trash comes out of it as it was deleted; refused while another enabled site routes one of its addresses, or one is in release quarantine, and only administrators bring a site out of the trash. A live site goes back to the saved revision given (history names them); its certificates and app are untouched. To set a trashed site back to an older revision, bring it out of the trash first.

mcp_tool_deploy.text: Puts the newest version online. An app (AP12) deploys in the background: an application or static site is built, runs its pre-deploy command and takes over once it answers over HTTP, a failed step leaving the old one serving; other kinds start again. Creating an app does not deploy it; variables and config files reach it only now. A stack (ST2) is rebuilt from its configuration, queued, and starts if stopped. Answers for an app a RUN code to follow with run_read.

mcp_code_deploy.text: The app or stack to deploy.

mcp_tool_roll_back.text: Puts back the release that served before the one serving now, without rebuilding, of an application or static site (AP12), or of a site (S20) running one (administrators). A failed deploy never served: the one before it still serves, and roll back goes one further back. Refused when nothing earlier is kept, or for other kinds. The pre-deploy command never runs: a database stays as the newer release left it. A stack (ST2) is queued back to its last good configuration. An app or site answers a RUN code for run_read; with drop an app's kept release is removed instead.

mcp_code_roll_back.text: The app, stack or site to roll back.

mcp_tool_power.text: Starts, stops or restarts an app (AP12), or stops a stack (ST2). An app's start brings it up as a deploy does; stop keeps its data, volumes and ports. An application's restart (or start) runs the release it serves again, without rebuilding or its pre-deploy command, unless its source or settings changed since: then it becomes a new release that runs the command. A stack only stops, dependents first, volumes kept; deploy starts it. It runs while the call waits, with no run to follow. Answers the state afterwards.

mcp_code_power.text: The app or stack to start, stop or restart.

mcp_action.text: Whether to start, stop or restart; an app already in the asked state is left as it is.

mcp_tool_back_up.text: Takes a backup now. An app (AP12) has its volumes copied, while the call waits and with the app stopped meanwhile, to the backup target chosen in its settings; refused without one, or for an app built from a repository. A database (DB12, administrators only) is dumped in the background to the installation's database backup target. How many are kept is one Backups setting for every app. Answers once an app's backup is made, or that a database's dump started.

mcp_code_back_up.text: The app or database to back up.

mcp_tool_app_exec.text: Runs one command inside the running app, beside its main process; the command can read and change the app's data. With console the line goes to the app's main process instead, as if typed in its console (a game's); a line equal to the template's stop command counts as a deliberate stop, so the app is not restarted as crashed. A command that runs longer than two minutes is answered as failed, yet it may keep running inside the app. Answers the exit code and the last 16 KiB of output, or with console only that the line was sent.

mcp_code_exec.text: The app to run the command in.

mcp_console.text: Sends the line to the app's main process instead of running a new program.

mcp_tool_variable_set.text: Sets runtime environment variables of an app (AP12), each named by its key. set gives plain values, secret values stored encrypted and never shown again, generate a random secret nobody sees, unset removes keys; a replaced or removed value cannot be got back, and one refusal writes nothing. The app sees changes at its next deploy. Give at least one of set, secret, generate, unset. Answers the keys changed, never a value.

mcp_code_variables.text: The app whose variables to change.

mcp_code_set.text: The app's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_app_application_set.text: Creates or changes an Application: a git repository built with a Dockerfile or Nixpacks, or a prebuilt image, released behind a health check; roll_back returns to the release before. Only an administrator creates one; anyone else uses app_create_from_template and changes only name and crash_policy. Creating does not deploy: call deploy. Changes, limits too, reach it at its next deploy. A deploy starts the new release beside the old, which serves until the drain ends; an exclusive volume stops the old first. Its variables are variable_set. A code of an app of another kind is refused, naming that kind's tool; change_kind: true turns it into this kind. Answers the new app's code, or what changed.

mcp_tool_app_docker_container_set.text: Creates or changes a Docker container app: one image run as it is; no build, health check or releases, so roll_back refuses it. Only an administrator creates one; anyone else uses app_create_from_template and changes only name and crash_policy. Creating does not start it: call deploy. image_app runs another app's image instead of its own. Changes reach it at its next deploy; memory_limit_mb and cpu_limit redeploy a running one at once. A deploy kills the running container before the new one starts; power stop and restart give it 10 s. Its variables are variable_set.
