A code of an app of another kind is refused, naming that kind's tool; change_kind: true turns it into this kind. Answers the new app's code, or what changed.

mcp_tool_app_static_site_set.text: Creates or changes a Static site app: a repository built by build_command, served as files. Only an administrator creates one; anyone else uses app_create_from_template and changes only name and crash_policy. Creating does not deploy: call deploy; changes reach it at its next deploy. A code of an app of another kind is refused, naming that kind's tool; change_kind: true turns it into this kind. Answers the new app's code, or what changed.

create_system_container_app_description.text: Creates a System container app from its settings through the panel's own create; nothing is started.

change_system_container_app_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a System container app through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

create_vm_app_description.text: Creates a Virtual machine app from its settings through the panel's own create; nothing is booted.

change_vm_app_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a Virtual machine app through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

create_workspace_app_description.text: Creates a Workspace app from its settings through the panel's own create; nothing is started.

change_workspace_app_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a Workspace app through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

app_runtime_image.text: The runtime image (RI5) the app runs inside; a workspace cannot do without one. A host that lacks the image's variant for its runtime refuses the deploy.

mcp_tool_app_system_container_set.text: Creates or changes a System container (LXC) on an Incus host: a whole Linux system that shares the host's kernel and keeps its disk; no releases. Only an administrator creates one; anyone else uses app_create_from_template and changes only name and crash_policy. Creating does not start it: deploy creates and starts it. Changes reach it at its next deploy; memory_limit_mb and cpu_limit redeploy a running one at once. Disks and network cards: app_device_set; once stopped, template_set from_app captures it. A code of an app of another kind is refused; change_kind: true turns it into this kind.

mcp_tool_app_vm_set.text: Creates or changes a Virtual machine on an Incus host: its own kernel, from a catalog or prepared image; set up by cloud_init on first boot. Only an administrator creates one; anyone else uses app_create_from_template and changes only name and crash_policy. Creating does not start it: deploy creates and boots it. Changes reach it at its next deploy; memory_limit_mb and cpu_limit redeploy a running one at once. host_media_set fetches ISOs, app_install_media_set puts one in its drive; disks: app_device_set. A code of an app of another kind is refused; change_kind: true turns it into this kind.

mcp_tool_app_workspace_set.text: Creates or changes a Workspace: a development box on a Docker or Incus host, run from a runtime image; only /home/site survives a deploy. With a repository, the code is checked out there, built and run with start_command. Only an administrator creates one; anyone else uses app_create_from_template and changes only name and crash_policy. Creating does not start it: call deploy, then site_app_set. Changes reach it at its next deploy; memory_limit_mb and cpu_limit redeploy a running one at once. A code of an app of another kind is refused; change_kind: true turns it into this kind.

mcp_tool_app_script_run.text: Runs a script of the template an app was made from, while the call waits. Script install runs the template's install step, or resumes or retries it, until the install is done; reinstall runs it again once installed or failed, as the template's data policy says: preserve keeps the volumes, clear first removes the container and its volumes, which cannot be undone. Both need a stopped app and an administrator; read AP12 shows the install state. Script update runs the template's update script inside the running app, changing no setting. Answers done, or the update script's output.

mcp_code_app_script_run.text: The app (AP12) made from a template whose script to run.

mcp_app_script.text: Which script: install, reinstall (as the template's data policy says) or update (inside the running app).

create_device_description.text: Attaches a disk or a network card to an app through the panel's own Devices tab.

change_device_description.text: Grows a disk of an app through the panel's own save; a device's name and kind never change.

device_app.text: The app (AP12) the device is attached to: a virtual machine or a system container.

instance_device_kind.text: A disk, or a network card (nic); install media is put in a machine's drive by its own action.

instance_device_name.text: Lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and dashes, 1 to 31 characters; root and eth0 are reserved.

instance_device_size.text: A disk's size in GB, at least 1; a disk only grows. It counts against the owner's disk quota.

mcp_tool_app_device_set.text: Attaches a disk or a network card to a virtual machine or system container, or grows a disk. A device's name and kind never change, so a change can only set a disk's size. The disk's size and the extra network card count against the owner's quota. Detaching is delete DV3, which deletes a disk's data. Install media (an ISO) is not a device here: app_install_media_set. Answers the device's code (DV3).

mcp_code_app_device_set.text: The device's code (DV3); leave out to attach one.

run_preview_description.text: Queues a preview deploy of one ref of an application, as the previews page's create does.

preview_app.text: The application (AP12) that builds from a git repository and that a site exposes.

preview_run_ref.text: The branch, tag or commit to build.

mcp_tool_preview_run.text: Starts a preview deploy of one branch, tag or commit of an application: a separate copy built from that ref in the background, at a generated address, until it expires. The same ref again refreshes that preview and extends its window. Refused unless the application builds from a git repository, a site exposes it and a preview base address is configured; a preview counts against its owner's preview limit. Ending it early is delete PV6. Answers the preview's code (PV6); read PV6 shows how far it is.

create_runtime_image_description.text: Creates a runtime image through the panel's own create.

change_runtime_image_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a runtime image of your own through the panel's own save.

runtime_image_name.text: The image's name (node-22), as apps and templates name it.

runtime_image_description.text: What the image carries, shown where an app picks it.

runtime_image_workdir.text: The folder an app's process starts in.

runtime_image_shell.text: The shell the console and app_exec use inside it.

runtime_image_enabled.text: False hides it from new apps and refuses apps that use it at their next deploy.

mcp_tool_runtime_image_set.text: Creates or changes a runtime image: what Workspaces and Applications run inside (such as Node 22), with the command, port and build command they use unless they set their own. Built-in images cannot be changed; create a new one with their values for a variant. Administrators only. Hohenheim never builds an image made here: docker_image and incus_image must already be on the hosts, or the deploy refuses. Answers the runtime image's code (RI5) and what changed.

mcp_code_runtime_image_set.text: The runtime image's code (RI5); leave out to create one.

create_template_description.text: Creates an app template through the catalog's own create; it is not approved.

change_template_description.text: Changes the settings sent of an app template through the catalog's own save.

template_name.text: The template's name, as people pick it.

mcp_tool_template_set.text: Creates or changes an app template: its kind, an install script run once, an update script, readiness and a graceful stop. approved true lets people make apps from it, false withdraws that; give it alone. from_app instead captures a stopped System container or Virtual machine; its disk becomes an image on its host (minutes), so the template works only there. Administrators only; others see it once approved. Variables: variable_set owner=TP3. Answers the template's code (TP3) and what changed.

mcp_code_template_set.text: The template's code (TP3); leave out to create one.

mcp_template_approved.text: True approves the template for people to make apps from, false withdraws the approval; given alone, with code.

mcp_template_from_app.text: A stopped System container or Virtual machine (AP12) to capture as a new template, instead of code.

import_template_description.text: Imports a template from an exported document or the shipped community catalog, as the import page does; it is not approved.

template_import_document.text: The JSON document template_export made; give it or catalog_app.

template_import_source.text: Where the document came from, kept on the template; with a document only.

template_import_catalog_app.text: An app of the community catalog shipped with Hohenheim; it becomes a System container template.

template_import_one.text: Give document or catalog_app, one of them.

template_import_source_document.text: source applies to a document only.

mcp_tool_template_import.text: Imports a template as a new one, from a document template_export made or from the community catalog shipped with Hohenheim. It never changes an existing template, and the new one is not approved: read it, then template_set approved=true. Administrators only. A document with a wrong checksum, another format or version, or an unknown kind, variable type or engine is refused and nothing is created. Give exactly one of document, catalog_app. Answers the new template's code (TP3).

export_template_description.text: Answers a template as the document its import reads, without its approval.

template_export_secret.text: {$code} holds secret values, so its export is not shown here; download it from the template's page in the panel (Export).

mcp_tool_template_export.text: Exports a template as a JSON document that template_import, here or on another Hohenheim, turns back into the same template: settings, scripts, readiness, stop, variables, config files, databases and volumes, with a checksum; not its approval. Administrators only. A template holding a secret value (a secret setting, a secret question's default, a config file) is refused, since a secret never leaves in a tool answer: download it from the panel's Templates page, Export.

generate_instance_secret_description.text: Has the server make a random secret for a key that holds no value yet; the value is never shown. The app sees it from its next deploy.

delete_game_domain_description.text: Deletes this game address mapping and the records it generated.

enable_site_description.text: Switches the site on, so its addresses answer again.

disable_site_description.text: Switches the site off: its addresses stop answering, while its settings and the app behind it are kept. The panel's own site is refused.

stop_forcing_https_description.text: Stops redirecting to HTTPS on the site's addresses that have no working certificate, so they answer over HTTP. Addresses with a working certificate are left alone.

clone_site_description.text: Makes a switched-off copy of the site under a new name, with its upstream, settings, sign-in provider and access list.

manage_update_site_description.text: Changes the site's name, description or whether it is on. Only the fields given change.

delete_site_description.text: Deletes the site and its preview deployments; its addresses stop answering. Its certificates and the app behind it are kept.

rollback_release_description.text: Rolls the site back to its application's retained release, through the same health check a deploy passes; it runs in the background. Refused when no earlier release is kept.

check_address_reach_description.text: Checks again whether the address reaches this server from outside, forgetting the last answer.

delete_access_rule_description.text: Deletes the access rule; deleting a group deletes every rule inside it.

build_hook_revoke_description.text: Revokes the build hook: its URL then answers as an unknown one. This cannot be undone; make a new hook instead.

delete_dns_zone_description.text: Deletes the DNS zone and its records; this server stops answering for it.

delete_dns_peer_description.text: Removes the DNS peer, so zones are no longer transferred to or from it.

delete_database_description.text: Deletes the database with its data: its own container and volume, or its database and user on a shared engine. Refused while an app still uses it. This cannot be undone.

delete_database_engine_description.text: Deletes the database engine: its container and the data volume its databases sat on are removed. Refused while databases still sit on it. This cannot be undone.

delete_database_dump_description.text: Deletes the dump: its file is removed from the backup target, then its record. Refused while it is still uploading.

stop_stack_description.text: Stops the stack's containers, the ones others depend on last. Volumes and settings are kept.

delete_stack_description.text: Deletes the stack: its containers and network are removed; its volumes stay on the host.

delete_stack_service_description.text: Deletes the service and its container from the stack. Refused while another service depends on it.

delete_server_description.text: Removes the host from this panel and withdraws this panel's trust on it; the host and what runs on it are not touched. Refused while records still use it.

delete_runtime_image_description.text: Deletes this custom runtime image from the list. Refused while an app uses it.

delete_project_description.text: Deletes the project and the roles it owns. Refused while the project still owns records.

remove_orphan_description.text: Removes the leftover container the reconciler found on the host. Volumes are never removed this way.

refresh_stack_description.text: Reads the stack's live state from its host and answers its status; it changes nothing.

test_git_provider_description.text: Tests the git connection by listing its repositories, and answers how many or why it failed; it changes nothing.

test_backup_target_description.text: Checks whether the backup target can be reached, and answers why not when it cannot; it changes nothing.

test_channel_description.text: Sends a test alert through the notification channel.

cordon_server_description.text: Cordons the host: no new work is placed on it, while what already runs there keeps running.

drain_server_description.text: Moves every app off this host, pausing it first if it still takes new apps: each is stopped, moved to another host and started there. An app that cannot move is named and left alone.

uncordon_server_description.text: Ends the host's cordon, so new work may be placed on it again.

reap_controller_objects_description.text: Removes the network objects other Hohenheim controllers left on this Incus host. Objects of this controller, and objects an app still uses, are never removed.

template_project.text: The project the new app belongs to.

certificate_name.text: The name the certificate is listed under; left empty, its first hostname.

site_name.text: The site's name, as the panel lists it.

site_description.text: A note about the site, for the people who manage it.

set_dns_records_description.text: Makes names and types of the zone hold exactly the values given, or removes them, all in one write; answers what changed per name and type.

list_dns_records_description.text: Reads the zone's records you may see, one line each, or the whole zone as zone-file text.

dns_records_set.text: One entry per name and type: name (@ for the zone, labels such as www, *.dev or _acme-challenge), type, ttl (left out, the zone's default, also on a record that had its own), remove, and values: each a value (A an IPv4 address, AAAA an IPv6 address, CNAME, NS, MX and SRV a hostname, TXT any text, CAA "0 issue letsencrypt.org", TLSA "usage selector type hex"), priority (MX and SRV), weight and port (SRV), enabled (default true) and dyndns (A and AAAA only: on keeps the update token or makes one, new_token makes a new one, off removes it).

dns_records_list_name.text: Only the records of this name, relative to the zone; @ for the zone itself.

dns_records_list_type.text: Only the records of this type.

dns_records_as_zone_text.text: Answer the whole zone as zone-file text instead; name and type are then refused.

dns_list_text_whole.text: as_zone_text answers the whole zone; leave name and type out.

dns_list_text_admin.text: Only an administrator reads a whole zone as text; leave as_zone_text out to read the records of names you manage.

create_site_app.text: Create a site serving an app

create_site_app_description.text: Creates a site serving one of your apps through the panel's own create; nothing is deployed.

change_site_app.text: Change a site serving an app

change_site_app_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a site serving an app through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

create_site_static_files_description.text: Creates a site serving a folder of the host through the panel's own create.

change_site_static_files_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a site serving files through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

create_site_proxy_description.text: Creates a site forwarding to a host and port or a socket through the panel's own create.

change_site_proxy_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a proxy site through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

create_site_redirect_description.text: Creates a site redirecting every request through the panel's own create.

change_site_redirect_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a redirect site through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

site_change_kind.text: Set true to turn the site of another kind named by code into this kind, keeping only the settings this kind takes; without it such a code is refused.

site_app.text: The app's code (AP12) the site serves; pointing the site at another app leaves the previous one running.

site_access_list.text: The access list's code (AL6) every request must pass before reaching the site.

site_kind_other.text: {$code} is a {$kind} site; change it with {$tool}, or give change_kind: true to turn it into this kind.

site_kind_other_untooled.text: {$code} is a {$kind} site; give change_kind: true to turn it into this kind.

create_address_description.text: Adds an address to a site through the panel's own create.

delete_address_description.text: Removes an address from its site through the panel's own delete; its hostname stops answering there.

delete_access_list_description.text: Deletes an access list through the panel's own delete, refused where the panel refuses it.

delete_protected_path_description.text: Removes a protected path from its site through the panel's own delete; its requests no longer pass its access list.

delete_path_redirect_description.text: Removes a path redirect from its site through the panel's own delete; the site serves that path itself again.

change_address_description.text: Changes the settings sent of an address through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

address_site.text: The site's code (S20) the address belongs to; an address never moves to another site.

address_certificate.text: The certificate's code (C8) served for this address; left out, Hohenheim picks a certificate it holds that covers the name.

header_entry_value.text: The header's value; empty removes the header.

mcp_code_site.text: The site's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_site_app_set.text: Creates or changes a site serving one of your apps (AP12); creating does not start the app (deploy it). With hostname the site's first address is made in the same call: order its certificate with certificate_order, and point the name at this host yourself (dns_record_set). Non-administrators change only name, enabled and description. A site of another kind given as code is refused unless change_kind is true. Answers the site's code, or on a change the settings written.

mcp_tool_site_static_files_set.text: Creates or changes a site serving a folder on the host Hohenheim runs on; for a static site built from a repository, use app_static_site_set. Without root_path it serves nothing; managed by a non-administrator it serves nothing until an administrator turns on trusted_upstream. With hostname the first address is made in the same call. Non-administrators change only name, enabled and description. A site of another kind given as code is refused unless change_kind is true. Answers the site's code, or on a change the settings written.

mcp_tool_site_proxy_set.text: Creates or changes a site forwarding requests to a host and port or a unix socket, not to Hohenheim's apps; without forward_host or socket every request answers 502. Managed by a non-administrator it reaches only public addresses unless trusted_upstream is on. With hostname the first address is made in the same call. Non-administrators change only name, enabled and description. A site of another kind given as code is refused unless change_kind is true. Answers the site's code, or on a change the settings written.

mcp_tool_site_redirect_set.text: Creates or changes a site that answers every request with a redirect to target_url. With hostname the first address is made in the same call, so visitors who type https:// are redirected once its certificate is ordered. Non-administrators change only name, enabled and description. A site of another kind given as code is refused unless change_kind is true. Answers the site's code, or on a change the settings written.

mcp_tool_address_set.text: Adds an address (a hostname such as shop.example.com) to a site, or changes one. A name another live site routes, or one in release quarantine, is refused. Make its DNS record yourself with dns_record_set. For HTTPS order a certificate with certificate_order address=D4; otherwise Hohenheim uses a certificate it holds that covers the name, unless certificate pins one. On a TLS passthrough site an address takes no path, headers, HSTS, forced HTTPS or certificate. Headers merge by name; remove: true takes one away. Answers the address's code, or on a change the settings written.

mcp_code_address.text: The address's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_certificate_order.text: Orders a Let's Encrypt production certificate, counted against its rate limits: for the names in hostnames, for one address (address=D4: its hostname and site name filled in), or again for an existing certificate (code=C8: its names and challenge filled in; send what changes). Needs Let's Encrypt switched on; at most 5 orders and renewals an hour. Challenge http needs each name pointing here already; wildcards need dns. A manual dns order waits for its TXT records, shown on the certificate's page in the panel: publish them, then call certificate_renew. Answers the certificate's code.

mcp_code_certificate_order.text: The certificate (C8) to order again; leave out to order a new one.

mcp_address_certificate_order.text: The address (D4) to order a certificate for: an exact name, not excluded from Let's Encrypt, on a site that is no TLS passthrough.

mcp_tool_certificate_renew.text: Renews a Let's Encrypt certificate now for the same names, as the nightly renewal would, or finishes its waiting manual DNS order once the TXT records are published; which one follows from the certificate. A manual order that waited past a restart of Hohenheim has expired: order again with certificate_order. Needs Let's Encrypt switched on; counts against the 5 orders and renewals an hour. Uploaded certificates are not renewed here. Answers the certificate's code, or the failure, which is also stored on the certificate.

mcp_code_certificate_renew.text: The certificate (C8) to renew or finish.

mcp_tool_test.text: Checks something now. An address (D4): whether its name reaches this Hohenheim from outside, forgetting the last answer; read the address for the result. A DNS zone (Z7): its health, as the zone's page checks it; a secondary zone has none to check. A backup target (BT1): whether it can be reached, and why not. A notification channel (NC2): sends it a test alert and says whether it was delivered, only handed off or not sent. A git connection (G3): lists its repositories and says how many, or why not. A stack (ST2): reads its live state back and answers its status. It changes nothing else.

mcp_code_test.text: The address, DNS zone, backup target, notification channel, git connection or stack to check.

mcp_tool_dns_record_list.text: Reads a zone's records, all or one name or type: name, type, TTL (or the zone default it uses), the value as a resolver prints it, and whether it is switched off, made by Hohenheim itself (a certificate proof) or updated by dynamic DNS. as_zone_text answers the whole zone as zone-file text instead, for administrators only. Someone who is no administrator sees the records of names they manage and records shared with them to view. A secondary zone's records are read from the server that keeps them, or from this server's copy when it cannot be asked; the first line says which.

mcp_code_dns_zone_read.text: The zone (Z7, or its origin such as example.com) whose records to read.

mcp_tool_dns_record_set.text: Sets a zone's records: each entry makes one name and type hold exactly its values, others removed; remove: true drops the name and type. All entries apply together or none. Records Hohenheim made itself cannot be changed. Someone who is no administrator sets only A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, SRV and TLSA records under names they manage. dyndns makes, keeps or drops a value's dynamic DNS token; a new token is never answered, but shown once to your account on the zone's Records tab. A secondary zone is set on the server keeping its records, without dyndns. Answers what changed per name and type.

mcp_code_dns_zone_set.text: The zone (Z7, or its origin such as example.com) whose records to set.

mcp_tool_dns_zone_set.text: Creates or changes a DNS zone this Hohenheim answers for: primary (its records kept and edited here) or secondary (a copy pulled from primary_peer). A new primary zone gets one apex NS record per declared nameserver. secondaries becomes exactly the peers listed (DP2): a newly listed Hohenheim peer makes its copy at once, refused when it cannot; any other is told to pull. An empty list removes every copy. Turning on dnssec makes a signing key: lodge the DS record with the registrar. Records: dns_record_set. Administrators only. Answers the zone's code.

mcp_code_dns_zone.text: The zone (Z7, or its origin such as example.com); leave out to create one.

create_dns_zone_description.text: Adds a DNS zone through the panel's own create, and links the secondaries listed.

change_dns_zone_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a DNS zone through the panel's own save, and makes its secondaries the list sent; every other setting stays as it is.

zone_primary_peer.text: The peer (DP2) a secondary zone is copied from and whose server keeps its records.

zone_secondaries.text: The peers (DP2) that keep a copy of this primary zone; the list replaces the stored one.

dns_secondaries_primary.text: Only a primary zone has secondaries; a secondary zone is itself a copy

record_secondary_zone_owner.text: This is a secondary zone: its records are kept on {$peer}, its primary. Change them there

dns_dyndns_no_account.text: A dynamic DNS token is shown once to the account making the call, and no account stands behind this one

dns_dyndns_address_only.text: dyndns applies only to A and AAAA records

dns_dyndns_refused.text: You may not change this record's dynamic DNS

dyndns_parked.text: An update token was made for {$record}; it is shown once to {$account} on the zone's Records tab in the panel, until {$until :datetime}. Routers send it as the HTTP Basic password to {$url}.

dyndns_disclosure_warning.text: Copy them now: they are shown only this once. A router sends its token as the HTTP Basic password.

listed_from_owner.text: Read from {$peer}, which keeps this zone's records.

owner_unreached.text: the server that keeps this zone's records could not be asked

forward_copy_later.text: This server's copy follows at its next transfer.

dns_forward_dyndns.text: Dynamic DNS tokens of a secondary zone are made on the server that keeps its records: set them there

dns_forward_unreachable.text: This zone's records are kept on {$peer}, which could not be reached, so nothing was changed. {$reason}

dns_forward_unanswered.text: This zone's records are kept on {$peer}, which did not answer after the change was sent: read them with dns_record_list before sending it again. {$reason}

dns_forward_not_primary.text: This zone's records are kept on {$peer}, which holds the zone as a copy too, so they cannot be changed from here

dns_forward_server_required.text: A forwarded record set names the server it comes from

dns_copy_older.text: {$peer} runs an older Hohenheim that cannot make its own copy of {$origin}, so it was not made a secondary: make the copy there by hand, pulling from this Hohenheim, then list it again

dns_copy_unreachable.text: {$peer} could not be asked to keep a copy of {$origin}, so it was not made a secondary: {$reason}

dns_copy_conflict.text: {$peer} already keeps a zone {$origin} of its own or copied from elsewhere, so it was not made a secondary: remove that zone there first

dns_copy_refused.text: {$peer} did not make a copy of {$origin}, so it was not made a secondary: {$reason}

mcp_tool_dns_zone_take_over.text: Moves a DNS zone's records to this Hohenheim from the Hohenheim keeping them, when this one holds the zone's copy: this one becomes its primary at the next serial, the other its secondary, copying from here; the other's own secondaries are linked here where they are peers. Every name keeps its answer throughout; if the other cannot take the copy, the move is undone. Refused, nothing changed, when the copy is not current, the other runs an older Hohenheim or holds no API key of this one, or the zone is signed. Dynamic DNS updates sent to the other keep working. Administrators only.

mcp_code_dns_zone_take_over.text: The secondary zone (Z7, or its origin such as example.com) to take over.

take_over_hint.text: Move this zone's records here from the Hohenheim keeping them, which then keeps a copy of it.

take_over_confirm.text: This Hohenheim will keep the zone's records and answer for it as its primary; the Hohenheim keeping them now becomes its secondary. Every name keeps its answer while it moves.

take_over_done.text: {$zone} is kept here now: {$records :integer} records at serial {$serial}; {$peer} keeps a copy.

take_over_done_unlinked.text: {$zone} is kept here now: {$records :integer} records at serial {$serial}; {$peer} keeps a copy. Not linked here, as they are no peers of this Hohenheim: {$unlinked}; they still copy the zone from {$peer}.

take_over_unconfirmed.text: {$zone} is kept here now ({$records :integer} records at serial {$serial}), but {$peer} did not confirm that it gave the zone up and could not be asked since. If {$peer} still holds it as primary, make it a secondary of this Hohenheim there; its records are kept here.

dns_take_over_not_secondary.text: {$zone} is no copy here: only a secondary zone is taken over

dns_take_over_owner_unknown.text: {$zone} is copied from {$peer}, which is no Hohenheim this one holds an API key of, so it cannot be taken over

dns_take_over_no_key.text: This Hohenheim shares no transfer key with {$peer}, so {$peer} could not copy {$zone} from here: agree one first (dns_peer_set negotiate_key)

dns_take_over_older.text: {$peer} runs an older Hohenheim that cannot hand {$zone} over; nothing was changed

dns_take_over_unreachable.text: {$peer} could not be asked about {$zone}, so nothing was changed: {$reason}

dns_take_over_unanswered.text: {$peer} did not answer about {$zone}, so nothing was changed: {$reason}

dns_take_over_not_primary.text: {$peer} does not keep the records of {$zone} itself, so it cannot hand the zone over; nothing was changed

dns_take_over_dnssec.text: {$zone} is signed with DNSSEC on {$peer}, and its signing key cannot move yet; nothing was changed

dns_take_over_behind.text: This copy of {$zone} is not current (serial {$copy} here, {$serial} on {$peer}): try again once it followed; nothing was changed

dns_take_over_not_linked.text: {$peer} does not list this Hohenheim as a secondary of {$zone} with the transfer key both keep, so it could not copy the zone from here; nothing was changed

dns_take_over_no_call_back.text: {$peer} holds no API key of this Hohenheim, so after the move it could not send record changes or dynamic DNS updates here: give its peer for this Hohenheim a base URL and key first; nothing was changed

dns_take_over_tied.text: {$zone} holds {$count :integer} records {$peer} made itself for its own apps ({$sources}); they cannot move yet, so nothing was changed

dns_take_over_undone.text: {$peer} did not take its copy of {$zone}, so the move was undone and the zone is a copy here again: {$reason}

restore_site_revision_description.text: Sets a live site back to one of its saved revisions through its history's own restore.

site_revision.text: The saved revision to set a live site back to, as history names it.

mcp_tool_database_move_to_shared.text: Moves a dedicated database onto its host's shared engine of the same kind, as a logical database with its own login; or, with cleanup_only, removes the old dedicated engine a move could not remove. The database must be running, on a kind with logical databases (not Redis). The move runs in the background (read DB12 shows Provisioning until done): every app attached to it is stopped during dump and restore, and the dump and old data volume are kept as a rollback. Answers that the move started, or that the old engine was removed.

mcp_cleanup_only.text: True moves nothing and only removes the dedicated engine an earlier move left behind; refused when no move left one.

mcp_tool_database_dump_restore.text: Restores a stored database dump: into a new dedicated database called name on the host of the database the dump came from (the source keeps running), or with in_place over that database, after a fresh dump of it. The dump must be complete; in place also needs its database to still exist. An in-place restore cannot be undone except by restoring that fresh dump. Administrators only. Answers a RUN code: follow it with run_read, which names the new database or the fresh dump.

mcp_in_place_dump.text: True replaces the source database's contents after a fresh dump of it; false restores into a new database called name.

mcp_tool_snapshot_restore.text: Puts a snapshot back: every volume of its app is replaced by the snapshot's contents, so files written since the snapshot are lost. The app is taken down meanwhile and a running one starts again after; a restore that fails part way leaves the app in error, not started. This cannot be undone; take a new snapshot first if what is there now matters. A snapshot that is not complete is refused. Answers that the snapshot was put back.

mcp_tool_app_move.text: Moves an app cold to another host: it stops, its container and volumes move, and it starts on the new host. Administrators only. Refused when the app is busy, already on that host, of a kind that cannot move, bound to a game address, publishing a host port, holding install media or devices the hosts cannot carry, taking its image from another app, using a database that runs on its old host (detach it first), or when the target host cannot take it. Answers the host it now runs on.

migrate_host_help.text: The host to move it to, by its code (SR1); a host that is not admitted or has no room is refused.

migrate_database_attached.text: {$name} uses the database {$database}, which stays on its host, so the app could not run beside it on the new one. Detach the database first.

restore_database_dump_description.text: Restores a complete dump into a new dedicated database on the host of the database it came from; the source keeps running.

restore_database_dump_in_place_descripti.text: Stores a fresh dump of the dump's database, then replaces its contents with the dump.

migrate_instance_description.text: Moves an app cold to another host: it stops, its container and volumes move, and it starts there.

change_snapshot_note_description.text: Changes the words kept with a snapshot; the snapshot itself stays as it was.

delete_backup_target_description.text: Deletes a backup target. Refused while a setting still names it; the backups already stored there stay where they are.

app_file_read_path_help.text: The file to read or the folder to list, as an absolute path under one of the app's volumes; left out, the first volume.

app_file_path_help.text: An absolute path under one of the app's volumes, such as /data/config.yml.

app_file_content_help.text: The file's new text; left out, the file is written empty.

app_file_to_help.text: The new absolute path under one of the app's volumes; something already there is refused.

app_file_read_description.text: Reads a file or lists a folder in the app's volumes, as the Files tab does.

app_file_write_description.text: Creates or replaces a file in the app's volumes with the given text, as the Files tab's editor saves it.

app_folder_make_description.text: Makes a folder in the app's volumes; something already there is refused.

app_file_delete_description.text: Deletes a file, link or whole folder tree in the app's volumes; it cannot be undone.

app_file_move_description.text: Renames or moves a file or folder inside the app's volumes.

mcp_tool_snapshot_set.text: Takes a snapshot of an app's volumes on its own host now, with an optional note to recognise it by (give the app's code), or changes a snapshot's note (give its code). The app is stopped while the copy is made and started again afterwards. A snapshot stays on the app's host; a backup that leaves the host is back_up. Refused for an app with no volumes or of a kind that cannot snapshot. Put it back with snapshot_restore; remove it with delete. Answers the snapshot's code (SN14).

mcp_code_snapshot_set.text: An app's code (AP12) to snapshot it, stopped while the copy is made; a snapshot's code (SN14) to change its note.

mcp_tool_app_file_read.text: Reads a file or lists a folder in an app's volumes, as the Files tab does. Paths are absolute paths inside the app's container under one of its volumes' mount points (for example /data/config.yml); left out, the first volume is listed, and every answer names all volume mount points. The app must be running. A file larger than the installation's file limit (8 MiB unless changed) is refused rather than cut; a folder with more entries than its listing limit (2000 unless changed) is refused rather than listed in part. A binary file is answered by its size only. Entries that are managed configuration files are marked. Nothing is changed.

mcp_code_app_file_read.text: The app (AP12) whose files to read.

mcp_tool_app_file_write.text: Writes in an app's volumes, as the Files tab does: creates or replaces a file with the given text, or with folder makes a folder. A replaced file's old content cannot be got back. A managed configuration file (one Hohenheim writes at every start) is refused. The app must be running. Deleting is app_file_delete. Answers the path written.

mcp_code_app_file_write.text: The app (AP12) whose files to change.

mcp_folder.text: True makes a folder at the path instead of writing a file; it takes no content.

mcp_tool_app_file_delete.text: Deletes a file, link or whole folder tree in an app's volumes, as the Files tab's delete does. A volume's root cannot be deleted, and a managed configuration file (or a folder holding one) is refused. The app must be running. This cannot be undone; take a snapshot first with snapshot_set if the data may matter. Answers the path deleted.

mcp_code_app_file_delete.text: The app (AP12) whose file or folder to delete.

mcp_tool_app_file_move.text: Renames or moves a file or folder inside an app's volumes; both paths must be inside the app's volumes and the target must not exist. A volume's root and a managed configuration file cannot be moved. The app must be running. Answers both paths.

mcp_code_app_file_move.text: The app (AP12) whose file or folder to move.

create_git_connection_description.text: Adds a git connection through the panel's own create.

change_git_connection_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a git connection through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

delete_git_connection_description.text: Removes a git connection, as the panel's Delete does; refused by name while an app builds from it.

mcp_tool_git_connection_set.text: Creates or changes a git connection apps build from: GitHub, GitLab or Gitea through their API with a token (or, for GitHub, an App key), or any git service over SSH with a private key. Credentials go in once, stored encrypted, and never come out. An SSH connection created without ssh_private_key gets a new key pair: the answer and read show its public_key, to add to the repository as a read-only deploy key; regenerate_key makes a new pair. A change sends only what changes. Only an administrator shares a connection with everyone. Answers the code (G2).

mcp_code_git_connection.text: The connection's code; leave out to create one.

git_connection_kind.text: How Hohenheim reaches the repositories: github, gitlab or gitea through their API with a token, ssh with a private key.

git_connection_repository.text: The repository the SSH key reaches, as git clones it over SSH, such as git@github.com:you/site.git.

git_connection_regenerate_key.text: Set true to replace the SSH key with a new pair; add the new public key to the repository, the old one stops working.

provider_ssh_public_key.text: Its public key, to add to the repository as a read-only deploy key: {$key}. Leave this empty to keep the key.

git_connection_key_twice.text: Give ssh_private_key or regenerate_key, not both.

create_database_description.text: Creates a managed database through the Databases page's own create; it is provisioned in the background.

change_database_description.text: Changes a database's memory and CPU ceilings through the Databases page's own save, or its password as the Change password button does.

create_database_engine_description.text: Creates a shared database engine through the engines page's own create; it comes up in the background.

change_database_engine_description.text: Changes a shared engine's memory and CPU ceilings through the engines page's own save.

create_database_link_description.text: Attaches a managed database to an app through the app's Attached databases tab.

change_database_link_description.text: Changes the variable prefix an attached database is given under; the app and the database stay.

create_backup_target_description.text: Creates a backup target through the settings page's own create.

change_backup_target_description.text: Changes what the call sends of a backup target through the settings page's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

mcp_tool_database_set.text: Creates a managed database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis or MongoDB) on a host, or changes its memory and CPU ceilings or its password. Its name, engine, placement, host and credentials are fixed once it exists. Someone who is no administrator may create one with name and engine only. It is provisioned in the background: read DB12 shows Provisioning until it serves. An app gets it only once attached (app_database_set) and deployed. A new ceiling recreates the container, so connections drop until it is back. Answers the code (DB12).

mcp_code_database_set.text: The database's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_database_engine_set.text: Creates a shared database engine on a host (one container that many databases live in as logical databases), or changes its memory and CPU ceilings. Its memory is booked on the host at once (a host without room refuses the create) and it comes up in the background (read DE3 shows when it serves). A new ceiling recreates the container, so every database on it loses its connections until it is back. Delete is refused while databases sit on it. Answers the code (DE3).

mcp_code_database_engine_set.text: The engine's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_app_database_set.text: Attaches a managed database to an app, which then sees its connection as variables under a prefix: DB gives DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_NAME and DB_URL, and the app's first attached database also gives DATABASE_URL. Only an app on a Docker host can take one, on the same host as the database. A change can only set the prefix. The variables reach the app at its next deploy. Detaching is delete DL2, which leaves the database and its data alone. Answers the attachment's code (DL2).

mcp_code_app_database_set.text: The attachment's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_backup_target_set.text: Creates or changes a backup target: where app backups and database dumps are written. Kind filesystem is a folder on this installation's own machine, which is not off-host unless the folder is mounted remote storage; kind ssh is a folder on another enrolled host, reached over SSH with its confirmed host key (a quarantined or unconfirmed host is refused when used). A change sends only what changes. Check it with test BT1. Administrators only. Answers the target's code (BT1).

mcp_code_backup_target_set.text: The target's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_backup_restore.text: Restores an app backup, in the background. By default into a new app while the app it came from keeps running; an administrator may pick the host (left out, a host with room is picked), anyone else gets the source app's own host. With in_place the backup replaces the data of the app it came from, after a fresh backup of that app is taken first; the data as it was before survives only in that fresh backup. A backup that is not complete is refused. Answers a RUN code: follow it with run_read.

mcp_in_place_backup.text: True replaces the source app's data instead of making a new app; a fresh backup is taken first.

database_generate_password.text: True sets a newly generated password that no answer shows; attached apps get it at their next deploy or restart.

database_engine_code.text: The shared engine (DE3) to put a shared database on; left out, the host's engine of its kind, created when missing.

database_host_code.text: The host (SR1) the database runs on; left out, this machine. It cannot change later.

database_engine_host_code.text: The host (SR1) the engine runs on; left out, this machine. It cannot change later.

database_link_app.text: The app (AP12) to attach the database to, on a Docker host.

database_link_database.text: The managed database (DB12) to attach, on the app's own host.

backup_target_host.text: The enrolled host (SR1) an SSH target writes to; only an SSH target takes it.

backup_restore_host.text: The host (SR1) the new app lands on; left out, a host with room is picked. Administrators only.

backup_target_name.text: The name the target is listed and picked by; no two targets share one.

database_password_twice.text: Give a password or ask for a generated one, not both.

restore_new_description.text: Restores the backup as a new app, on the host you pick or one with room; the backup's own app keeps running.

restore_in_place_description.text: Takes a fresh backup of the backup's app, then replaces that app's volumes with the backup's; its settings, variables and config files stay.

mcp_tool_host_admission_set.text: Decides whether a host takes new apps. state=admitted runs every preflight check and admits a waiting host once the required ones pass, checks an admitted host again, or ends a pause. state=paused stops new apps landing on the host while what runs there keeps running; move_apps_off=true also stops each app, moves it to another host and starts it there, naming any that cannot move. Admitting again does not move them back. Answers what happened, with how many apps moved and which were refused.

mcp_host_state.text: admitted checks and admits a waiting host, re-checks an admitted one, or ends a pause; paused takes no new apps.

mcp_move_apps_off.text: True also moves every app off the host, pausing it first; only with state=paused.

mcp_tool_host_trust.text: Pins and confirms the key a host is known by: its SSH host key (kind ssh) or its Incus daemon's certificate (kind incus). Without fingerprint it reads the key the host presents now and pins it, unconfirmed; ask the machine's person to read its fingerprint on the machine ('incus info' for Incus) and compare. Giving the pinned fingerprint confirms it; giving that of a CHANGED key adopts it, unconfirmed, and unadmits the host. Adopt a change only when you know why: it is what a man-in-the-middle looks like. Answers the fingerprint and what was done.

mcp_trust_kind.text: ssh is the SSH host key (a host with an SSH target); incus is the Incus daemon's certificate (reached over https).

mcp_tool_host_client_key_reset.text: Gives Hohenheim a new client identity for one host: a new SSH client key (kind ssh) or a new Incus client certificate (kind incus). On SSH the old key stops at once and the host is unreachable until the machine's person puts the new public key (read shows it) in authorized_keys on the machine. On Incus the old certificate works until its trust entry is removed on the daemon; enrol the new one there. This cannot be undone. Answers that a new key or certificate was made.

mcp_client_key_kind.text: ssh makes a new SSH client key; incus makes a new Incus client certificate. A kind the host lacks is refused.

mcp_tool_host_leftover_cleanup.text: Removes, from one Incus host, the shared objects (isolation ACL, extra-NIC bridge, presence marker) that OTHER Hohenheim controllers left behind, including those with no presence stamp, which the scheduled sweep never touches. Objects this Hohenheim owns are never removed, and the daemon refuses to remove one still in use. This cannot be undone; old images are image_cleanup. Answers how many objects were removed and how many were refused.

mcp_code_incus_host.text: The Incus host, by its code (SR1).

mcp_tool_image_cleanup.text: Starts the image cleanup on every host that runs a stack, now instead of at its nightly run: dangling images and superseded versions of the images stacks use are removed. Images in use, and images newer than the minimum age the apps settings keep, stay; a removed image is pulled again by the next deploy that needs it. Administrators only. What other Hohenheims left on an Incus host is host_leftover_cleanup. Answers at once that it started; what it removed shows only in Hohenheim's own log.

mcp_tool_host_media_set.text: Puts an install medium (an ISO a new virtual machine boots from) on an Incus host by fetching it from a public URL, or removes one. It needs the right to manage install media. A fetch is checked at once, then downloads in the background; the host's Install media tab shows its progress, and a virtual machine can use the medium once it is there. An existing medium is never replaced: remove it first. One attached to an app cannot be removed; removing cannot be undone. Uploading an ISO is panel-only. Answers that the fetch started or the medium was removed.

mcp_code_media_host.text: The Incus host that holds the medium, by its code (SR1).

mcp_remove_media.text: True removes the medium named name from the host; it takes no url.

mcp_tool_stack_volumes_purge.text: Tears a stack down and destroys every volume the stack owns; volumes made outside the stack (external names in a service's mounts) are left alone. The data is gone for good; the next deploy rebuilds the stack with empty volumes. The purge is queued on the stack's worker; the stack's history shows it once it settled. Answers that the purge was queued.

mcp_code_stack_purge.text: The stack whose own volumes to destroy (ST2).

trust_host_key.text: {$actor} pinned or trusted the SSH host key of {$subject}

trust_host_key_description.text: Reads and pins the SSH host key a host presents, confirms the pinned one, or adopts a changed one, by the fingerprint compared on the machine.

trust_incus_cert.text: {$actor} pinned or trusted the Incus certificate of {$subject}

trust_incus_cert_description.text: Reads and pins the certificate an Incus daemon presents, confirms the pinned one, or adopts a changed one, by the fingerprint compared on the machine.

trust_fingerprint.text: The fingerprint you compared on the machine: the pinned one confirms it, the presented one adopts that key.

trust_fingerprint_unknown.text: {$fingerprint} is neither the pinned fingerprint nor the one {$name} presents now; nothing was trusted.

fetch_host_media.text: {$actor} started fetching an install medium onto {$subject}

fetch_host_media_description.text: Checks an ISO's public URL, then downloads it onto an Incus host in the background as a named install medium.

delete_host_media_description.text: Deletes an install medium no app has attached from an Incus host.

media_name.text: The medium's name, by which a virtual machine's install-media device names it.

media_url.text: Where to download the ISO from; a private-network address is refused.

stack_move_deployed.text: Destroy the stack's containers before moving it to another host; the next deploy would leave them running on the old one

stack_move_unverifiable.text: Cannot verify the stack has no containers left (Docker is unreachable); move refused

create_host_description.text: Adds a host through the Hosts page's own create, enrolling its Incus certificate when a trust token is given.

change_host_description.text: Changes what the call sends of a host through the Hosts page's own save, or accepts its posture's risk as the Accept risk button does.

create_project_description.text: Creates a project through the Projects page's own create, with its own membership role.

change_project_description.text: Changes a project's name or description through the Projects page's own save.

create_environment_description.text: Creates an environment of a project through the Environments page's own create.

change_environment_description.text: Changes an environment's name, description or project through the Environments page's own save.

create_stack_description.text: Creates a stack through the Stacks page's own create; nothing is deployed.

change_stack_description.text: Changes what the call sends of a stack through the Stacks page's own save; a rename or a new host is refused while it has containers.

create_stack_service_description.text: Creates a service of a stack through the stack's Services tab; it starts at the stack's next deploy.

change_stack_service_description.text: Changes what the call sends of a stack service through its own save; it reaches the container at the stack's next deploy.

mcp_tool_host_set.text: Adds a host (a machine apps run on: Docker over SSH, or Incus over HTTPS or its local socket) or changes one; adding grants Hohenheim root-equivalent control of it. A new host takes no apps until trusted (host_trust) and admitted (host_admission_set). Two steps are done on the machine itself, so ask its person: put the client public key read shows in authorized_keys there (SSH), and read the host's key fingerprint there to compare in host_trust. The local host's name, runtime, SSH target and Incus URL cannot change. Answers the code (SR1).

mcp_code_host_set.text: The host's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_project_set.text: Creates a project (a group of apps, sites and databases that share members and environments) or changes its name and description. Someone who is no administrator sees the projects they are a member of but cannot create or change one. A new project gets its own membership role, which cannot be swapped later; people join it through that role or by sharing. Environments are environment_set. Delete is refused while the project still owns records or environments. Answers the code (PR3).

mcp_code_project_set.text: The project's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_environment_set.text: Creates an environment of a project (production, staging and so on: a named set of variables that apps of that project deploy with) or changes its name, description or project. An app joins an environment through its own settings. An environment that apps or variables still use cannot move to another project, and delete is refused while they use it. Answers the environment's code (EN4).

mcp_code_environment_set.text: The environment's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_stack_set.text: Creates a stack (container services deployed together on one host, like a compose project) or changes one. Creating starts nothing now: add services with stack_service_set, then deploy it; a stack with enabled=true none of whose services has a container yet is also deployed at every Hohenheim start. The name is part of every container, network and volume name, so a rename is refused while containers exist, and so is a new host: tear it down first. Answers the code (ST2).

mcp_code_stack_set.text: The stack's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_stack_service_set.text: Creates or changes one service of a stack: its image, command, environment, added Linux privileges, mounts, ports, dependencies, health check, restart policy and ceilings. A change reaches the running container only at the stack's next deploy. The name is the container's DNS name on the stack network; a service another one depends on cannot be renamed or disabled. environment replaces the whole set, as the panel's form does. Deleting is delete, which takes its container down. Answers the code (SS12).

mcp_code_stack_service_set.text: The service's code; leave out to create one.

accept_posture.text: The host's name, typed to accept that its shared containers let hostile tenants share one kernel; only with code, recorded against you.

accept_posture_name.text: accept_posture must be the host's name exactly ({$name}).

host_name.text: The host's name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes; 'local' is reserved for this machine.

host_ssh_target.text: How Hohenheim reaches the host over SSH, [user@]host[:port]; for Incus an optional admin shell.

host_runtime.text: What runs apps on the host: docker, reached through ssh_target, or incus, reached through incus_url.

project_title.text: The project's name, also shown in front of its environments' names.

environment_title.text: The environment's name, shown as "<project> / <name>" outside its project.

environment_project_code.text: The project it belongs to (PR3); a move is refused while apps or variables use the environment.

stack_enabled.text: True also deploys the stack at each Hohenheim start while none of its services has a container yet.

stack_registry_user.text: The login name for the registry the stack's private images are pulled from.

stack_registry_password.text: Password or token for the registry; stored encrypted and never shown again.

stack_about.text: Free text shown under the stack's name.

stack_host_code.text: The host the stack deploys to (SR1); left out, this machine. A move is refused while it has containers.

stack_service_stack_code.text: The stack the new service belongs to (ST2); it cannot change later.

service_enabled.text: False keeps the service out of the stack's next deploy; refused while another service depends on it.

service_mounts.text: The stack's own volumes, outside ones or memory mounted into the container; the list replaces every mount.

service_ports.text: Ports the container publishes on its host; a host port left out is allocated at deploy. The list replaces every port.

service_depends_on.text: Services of the same stack this one waits for at deploy, until started or healthy; the list replaces them all.

service_health_interval.text: Seconds between two health checks of the container.

service_health_timeout.text: Seconds one health check may take before it counts as failed.

service_health_retries.text: Failed checks in a row before the service counts as unhealthy.

service_health_start_period.text: Seconds after start during which failed checks do not count.

service_restart_policy.text: When Docker restarts the container after it exits; no never restarts it.

create_site_stream_description.text: Creates a TCP/UDP stream site forwarding public ports through the panel's own create.

change_site_stream_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a TCP/UDP stream through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

mcp_tool_site_stream_set.text: Creates or changes a TCP/UDP stream: public ports on the proxy's host, each forwarded unread to a port of forward_host, with no address and no HTTPS. One site carries every port of one service; ports merge by listen_port, remove: true drops one. A port another site or program holds is refused, naming it; switched off, the stream keeps its ports. Its access list may hold network rules only. Non-administrators change only name, enabled and description. A site of another kind given as code is refused unless change_kind is true. Answers the site's code, or on a change the settings written.

mcp_tool_site_ports_move.text: Moves every public port of a TCP/UDP stream (code) into another stream (into) that forwards to the same address, follows the same access list and is switched the same way, then sends the emptied stream to the trash, all in one go. The ports keep listening, so open connections stay; new ones take the other stream's connect timeout. Only an administrator moves ports. Restoring the trashed stream is refused while another site holds its ports. Answers which ports moved, from which stream into which.

mcp_code_site_ports_move.text: The stream (S20) whose ports move; it goes to the trash.

move_site_ports.text: {$actor} moved the ports of {$subject} into another stream

move_site_ports_description.text: Moves every public port of this stream into another stream forwarding to the same address and sends this one to the trash, in one go; the ports keep listening.

move_ports_confirm.text: Move every public port of this stream into another stream that forwards to the same address? This stream then goes to the trash; its ports keep listening, so open connections stay.

move_ports_into.text: The stream (S20) that takes the ports: it forwards to the same address, follows the same access list and is switched the same way.

site_ports_move_no_stream.text: {$target} is no TCP/UDP stream, so it cannot take the ports of {$name}.

site_ports_move_itself.text: Pick another stream: {$name} cannot take its own ports.

site_ports_move_other_address.text: {$target} forwards to {$address}, not to where {$name} forwards. Ports move only between streams that forward to the same address.

site_ports_move_other_access.text: {$target} and {$name} follow different access lists. Give both the same list first, so no moved port admits other clients.

site_ports_move_other_switch.text: One of {$target} and {$name} is switched off. Switch both on, or both off, first, so no moved port stops or starts forwarding.

create_volume_description.text: Declares a volume on an app through its Volumes tab's own form; it reaches the app at its next deploy.

change_volume_description.text: Changes a volume's mount path, size limit or exclusivity through its own form; its name never changes.

set_app_config_file_description.text: Creates, changes or removes the config file at a path of an app, as its Provisioning tab does.

set_template_config_file.text: {$actor} set a config file of template {$subject}

set_template_config_file_description.text: Creates, changes or removes the config file at a path of a template, as its Contents tab does.

set_stack_config_file.text: Set a stack service's config file
{$actor} set a config file of stack service {$subject}

set_stack_config_file_description.text: Creates, changes or removes the config file at a path of a stack service, as its Files tab does.

create_schedule_description.text: Creates an app's schedule and its chain of steps, as its Schedules tab does.

change_schedule_description.text: Changes a schedule's timing or switch, or replaces its whole chain of steps.

run_schedule_description.text: Runs an enabled schedule's chain now, as its Run now button does.

delete_schedule_description.text: Deletes a schedule with its chain of steps and the history of its runs; it no longer fires.

mcp_tool_volume_set.text: Declares a volume of an app (AP12) or changes one (VO5). Its name is its directory on the host, so it never changes and a volume never moves to another app; its mount path, size limit and exclusivity can change, reaching the app at its next deploy. Remove one with delete VO5, which destroys its data. Administrators only. Answers the volume's code (VO5).

mcp_code_volume_set.text: The volume's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_config_file_set.text: Sets a configuration file Hohenheim writes into a container before every start: of an app (AP12), of a template (TP3; apps made from it afterwards get it) or of a stack service (SS12). A file is named by its owner and path: the same path again changes it, remove takes it away. The content is stored encrypted and never read back; its \{\{KEY\}\} placeholders are filled from the variables. A change reaches a running app at its next deploy. A file in a volume Hohenheim does not manage is app_file_write.

mcp_code_config_file_owner.text: The app, template or stack service the file belongs to, by its code.

mcp_tool_schedule_set.text: Creates or changes a schedule on an app: a cron expression, read in a time zone, that runs a chain of steps in order, each after a delay. steps given is the whole chain, replacing the old one. Steps run with the authority of whoever last changed the schedule. A step the app cannot run, such as a back up of an app built from a repository, is refused at save. A changed cron, zone or switch re-arms it from now. Answers the schedule's code (SC4).

mcp_code_schedule_set.text: The schedule's code; leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_schedule_run.text: Runs an app schedule's chain now, only while the schedule is on; needs the right to configure the app. Answers the run's code (SCR9) and how it ended; read SCR9 shows it again.

volume_owner.text: The app (AP12) the volume belongs to; it cannot change later.

config_file_remove.text: Removes the file and its stored content; it is no longer written at the next start.

schedule_app.text: The app (AP12) the schedule acts on; it cannot change later.

schedule_steps.text: The whole chain in run order. Each step: action, delay_seconds after the previous step, on_failure (abort stops the chain, continue goes on, retry tries retries more times), and command for a console_command step or note for a snapshot step.

schedule_step_input.text: {$entry} does not apply to a {$action} step.

create_site_passthrough_description.text: Creates a site passing TLS untouched to a backend through the panel's own create.

change_site_passthrough_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a TLS passthrough site through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

mcp_tool_site_passthrough_set.text: Creates or changes a site that passes TLS connections untouched to a backend, chosen by the requested name; the backend presents its own certificate, so Hohenheim orders none. It takes no access list or sign-in provider, and its addresses take no path, headers, HSTS, forced HTTPS or certificate. Non-administrators change only name, enabled and description. A site of another kind given as code is refused unless change_kind is true. Answers the site's code, or on a change the settings written.

create_site_dev_namespace_description.text: Creates a dev namespace, a wildcard address dev machines register under, through the panel's own create.

change_site_dev_namespace_description.text: Changes the settings sent of a dev namespace through the panel's own save; every other setting stays as it is.

mcp_tool_site_dev_namespace_set.text: Creates or changes a dev namespace: a wildcard address such as *.dev.example.com where dev machines register over the dev tunnel, each taking one label. hostname gets no certificate: order a wildcard one with certificate_order. A registration_token left out on create is made by Hohenheim and shown once to the account that made this call (the key's owner), on the site's Dev sessions tab in the panel, for 24 hours; regenerate_registration_token replaces a lost one the same way. Non-administrators change only name, enabled and description. A site of another kind given as code is refused unless change_kind is true. Answers the site's code and, when a token was made, who sees it where and until when; a change answers the settings written.

site_sign_in_provider.text: The sign-in provider (SP3) every visitor must pass before reaching the site.

create_protected_path_description.text: Protects a path of a site with a list picked or made from the people, networks or provider given, as the site's own Protect a path does.

change_protected_path_description.text: Moves a protected path or points it at another access list through its own form.

mcp_tool_protected_path_set.text: Protects one path prefix of a site (such as /wp-admin), or changes a protection: requests under it must also pass an access list, on top of what the site requires. Give the list as access_list, or give credentials, networks or sign_in_provider to make an unshared list named after the site and path, one rule per entry, whose rules access_rule_set changes. A change moves the path or points it at another list. TLS passthrough sites and streams have no paths. Give at most one of access_list, credentials, networks, sign_in_provider. Answers the PP code.

mcp_code_protected_path_set.text: The protected path's code; leave out to create one.

credential_list.text: The people who may pass, each a username without a colon and a password; passwords are stored hashed and never shown.

protected_path_sign_in_provider.text: The sign-in provider (SP3) visitors must pass to reach the path.

protected_path_site.text: The site (S20) one of whose paths is protected; it cannot change later.

protected_path_list.text: An access list (AL6), shared or one you manage, that requests under the path must pass.

protected_path_one_guard.text: Give at most one of access_list, credentials, networks or sign_in_provider.

protected_path_no_http.text: A TLS passthrough site or a stream sees no paths, so none of its paths can be protected.

create_path_redirect_description.text: Adds a redirect of one path of a site through its Redirects tab's own form.

change_path_redirect_description.text: Changes a path redirect's path, match, target or status through its own form.

mcp_tool_path_redirect_set.text: Redirects one path of a site to another path or URL, or changes such a redirect: a request for from_path (only that path, or with path_match prefix everything under it) is answered with a redirect before the site's own handler, sign-in or access list runs, whatever kind of site it is. One redirect per site and path; a target that would send visitors back to the same redirect is refused. To redirect a whole address, use site_redirect_set. Answers the RD code.

mcp_code_path_redirect_set.text: The redirect's code; leave out to create one.

path_redirect_site.text: The site (S20) the redirect belongs to, whatever its kind; it cannot change later.

path_redirect_status.text: The HTTP status of the redirect: 301 and 308 permanent, 302 and 307 temporary.

set_site_revision_mark_description.text: Places or lifts a pin, a label or a hold on a saved revision of a site, as its History tab does.

mcp_tool_site_revision_mark_set.text: Places or removes a mark on a saved revision of a site: pinned keeps it, label names it in your words, hold keeps it for a legal or audit reason. A marked revision is never pruned from the site's kept revisions; a hold without revision covers the whole site and keeps every revision. One mark of each kind per revision; placing a label or hold again replaces its words. A hold needs the hold right, a pin or label the right to change the site. Revisions and marks are read with history. Answers the marks now in force there.

mcp_code_site_revision_mark.text: The site (S20) whose revision is marked.

revision_mark_revision.text: The revision marked, as history lists it; left out, a hold covers the whole site and a pin or label is refused.

revision_mark_kind.text: Which mark: pinned keeps the revision, label names it in your words, hold keeps it for a legal or audit reason.

revision_mark_text.text: The label's words, or the hold's reason; a pin takes none.

revision_mark_remove.text: Lift this mark from this revision (or the whole-site hold) instead of placing it.

revision_mark_no_text.text: Only a label or a hold carries words; a {$mark} mark takes none.

revision_mark_not_in_force.text: That mark is not in force there, so there is nothing to lift.

create_access_list_description.text: Creates an access list through the Access lists page's own form; it has no rules yet.

change_access_list_description.text: Changes an access list's name, how its rules combine or whether it is shared, through its own form.

mcp_tool_access_list_set.text: Creates or changes an access list: a named set of rules (networks, passwords, sign-in) a site, a protected path or a stream can require. satisfy says whether one passing rule is enough or all must pass; the rules themselves are added with access_rule_set. A new list has no rules, and a list with no rule switched on lets every visitor through: a protected path refuses such a list. Anyone who manages a site may make a list and then manages it; only administrators may share a list with everyone. Answers the AL code.

mcp_code_access_list_set.text: The access list's code; leave out to create one.

access_list_name.text: What tells this list apart from others in every picker.

access_list_satisfy.text: any: a single passing rule lets the request in. all: every rule must pass.

create_access_rule_description.text: Adds a rule, filled in and switched as given, at the top of an access list or inside a group, as the Rules tab's add does.

change_access_rule_description.text: Changes what a rule checks or whether it counts; a new kind replaces its fields.

mcp_tool_access_rule_set.text: Adds a rule to an access list, or changes one: a group (nested rules with their own satisfy), a password, an allowed or denied network, or a sign-in provider. A new rule is appended at the top level of access_list or inside group; give one of them. A rule switched on must be complete; one switched off may stay an incomplete draft and is ignored. A change that would leave a protected path's list with no rule switched on is refused. Changing kind replaces the rule's fields. Answers the RU code.

mcp_code_access_rule_set.text: The rule's code; leave out to create one.

access_rule_list.text: The list (AL6) whose top level gets the new rule; give this or group.

access_rule_group.text: A rule of kind group (RU9) the new rule goes inside; give this or access_list.

rule_sign_in_provider.text: The sign-in provider (SP3) the visitor must be signed in through.

access_rule_where.text: Give access_list for a rule at the list's top level, or group for one inside a group, not both.

create_sign_in_provider_description.text: Creates a sign-in provider of a kind through the Sign-in providers page's own form.

change_sign_in_provider_description.text: Changes what is sent of a sign-in provider through its own form; a secret left out stays as stored.

mcp_tool_sign_in_provider_set.text: Creates or changes a sign-in provider that sites, protected paths and access rules can make visitors pass: built-in passwords (kind basic, HTTP basic sign-in against credentials) or a Proteus identity service (kind proteus), which admits only identities holding required_permission. For basic, credentials is the whole list: usernames left out are removed for good, and an empty password keeps the stored one. A Proteus provider without endpoint, realm_client and access_key refuses every visitor. Administrators only. Answers its code (SP3).

mcp_code_sign_in_provider_set.text: The sign-in provider's code; leave out to create one.

set_ban_description.text: Bans an address from web traffic for a while or for good, or lifts every ban of it in force, as the Bans page does.

mcp_tool_ban_set.text: Bans an IP address from all sites' web traffic, for a while or for good, or lifts a ban; enforced in the firewall and the proxy at once. Only Hohenheim itself makes SSH bans, after SSH attacks. An IPv6 address bans its whole /64. Loopback, private and link-local addresses, this installation's own and those on the never-ban list cannot be banned. remove lifts every ban of the address in force, web and SSH alike; lifted bans stay in the list. Banning it again resets its end to duration in one step that never leaves it unbanned; an SSH ban of it stays. Administrators only. Answers when the ban ends, or that it was lifted.

ban_set_ip.text: The literal IP address to ban, or whose bans to lift; no hostname.

ban_set_reason.text: Why it is banned, as the list shows it; up to 255 characters.

ban_set_duration.text: How long the ban lasts; permanent holds until lifted.

ban_set_remove.text: Lift every ban of the address in force instead: it reaches every app again right away.

ban_set_remove_reason.text: reason applies to a ban, not to lifting one.

ban_set_for_good.text: {$ip} is banned for good, until the ban is lifted.

ban_set_lifted.text: Every ban of {$ip} is lifted: it reaches every app again.

regenerate_registration_token.text: {$actor} made a new registration token for {$subject}

regenerate_registration_token_descriptio.text: Gives a dev namespace a new registration token, shown once to the account that asked on the site's Dev sessions tab; a dev machine still presenting the old one is refused from then on.

regenerate_registration_token_confirm.text: Every dev machine still presenting the current token is refused from now on. The new token is shown to you once, on the Dev sessions tab.

registration_token_made.text: The registration token was made; it is shown once to {$account} on this site's Dev sessions tab in the panel, until {$until :datetime}.

registration_token_disclosure_warning.text: Copy it now: it is shown only this once. A dev machine presents it when it registers over the dev tunnel.

registration_token_no_account.text: A registration token Hohenheim makes is shown once to the account making the call, and no account stands behind this one: give registration_token yourself

site_regenerate_registration_token.text: Set true to replace the registration token with a new one Hohenheim makes, shown once as a made one is; every dev machine still using the old one is refused. Give nothing else with it.
