settings_set_description.text: Changes the settings of one section of the settings page, {$section}, as the page saves them.

settings_read_description.text: Reads one section of the settings page, each setting with its value, its default and where it comes from, as the page shows it.

mcp_settings_section.text: The section to read, named as on the settings page; signin is Sign-in, spam the spam service's own, brand Name and look.

mcp_tool_settings_read.text: Reads one section of this Hohenheim's settings as the settings page shows it: each setting by the argument its settings_<section>_set tool takes, with its label, value, default and where the value comes from, why you may not change it where you may not (set on the host only, overridden, a right you lack), and whether a change waits for a restart; then the section's revision, which a change takes as revision. A secret reads only as set or not set. Settings you may not read are left out; the spam section reads nothing while the spam service does not answer. It changes nothing.

mcp_tool_settings_general_set.text: Changes the General settings: public connections, what a hostname no site serves gets, the HTTPS redirect and visitors' error pages. unknown_hosts needs its target set in this or an earlier call. proxy_protocol_trusted_sources, unknown_hosts_forward and trusted_proxy_keys also need the right to edit trusted installation settings, which is never delegated. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_settings_https_set.text: Changes the HTTPS settings: automatic Let's Encrypt certificates, the Let's Encrypt account's email address, the staging switch and the DNS-01 wait. Turning staging on makes new certificates untrusted by browsers; existing ones stay until they renew. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_settings_backups_set.text: Changes the Backups settings: how many database dumps, app backups and snapshots are kept, the size caps of a dump and a volume archive, and when a missing backup raises an attention item. A lower retention deletes the oldest beyond it for good when the next one completes. Backup targets are backup_target_set. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_settings_notifications_set.text: Changes how this Hohenheim delivers alerts: retries, the sweep, the webhook timeout, inline delivery, the notifications hub and watch summaries. It needs the right to change the communication settings, which the administrator right does not include; the hub settings need the right to change them, never delegated. Where alerts go is notification_channel_set. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_settings_dns_set.text: Changes the DNS settings: the name this installation gives DNS peers, the nameserver hostnames published for primary zones, and the response rate limit. New nameservers do not rewrite existing zones' NS records: they set what new primary zones and zone imports get, and what the delegation check compares against. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_settings_blocking_set.text: Changes the Blocking settings: container process and log limits, the released-hostname quarantine, how hostname scans and other security events add up to automatic IP bans, the never-ban list, and how spam-service reputation feeds bans. Single bans are ban_set; never_ban protects an IP address from manual bans too. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_settings_apps_set.text: Changes the Apps and deploys settings: the build sandbox, release health gate and drain, previews, file manager bounds, stack image cleanup, and default per-owner quotas, where 0 means no cap (quota_set overrides them; there 0 allows nothing). builder_image and detector_image need the right to edit trusted installation settings, never delegated. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_settings_hosts_set.text: Changes the Hosts settings: the memory each host keeps for itself, the memory overcommit ratio, how old a host's memory reading and last contact may be before it takes no new apps, and the cleanup of what other Hohenheims left on shared Incus hosts. These decide where new apps go; apps already on a host stay. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_settings_signin_set.text: Changes the Sign-in settings: how long sessions last on sites behind a sign-in provider, and this panel's Proteus single sign-on. The Proteus settings also need the right to edit trusted installation settings, which is never delegated, and a restart. Proteus sign-in is offered only when its required_permission is set. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_settings_brand_set.text: Changes the Name and look settings: the name people see in headers, titles and messages, the logos and browser icon, the tint colour, theme fine-tuning, where the name in the header leads, the sidebar tone, the theme and brightness a first visit gets, and who runs this installation. It needs the right to change the brand settings. A page shows a change the next time it loads. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_settings_installation_set.text: Changes the Installation settings: this Hohenheim's name among linked Hohenheims, whether access and hostname-miss logs go to file, and the process limit of host processes it runs as another host account. Which parts this Hohenheim runs (proxy, DNS, firewall, stacks, databases, apps) is set on the host only. Only the settings given change; null resets one to its default. A setting set on the host only is refused by name; settings_read shows it. Answers the settings changed, those waiting for a restart, and the new revision.

mcp_tool_access_rule_move.text: Moves a rule one place up or down among its siblings (inside its group, or at the list's top level). The order never changes who gets in. It only decides what a visitor who has not signed in yet is asked for: the first rule that waits for a credential asks for its own (a password or a sign-in). A rule already first cannot move up, nor the last down, and it never leaves its group or list. Answers the rule it moved; list kind=access_rule shows the order.

mcp_code_access_rule_move.text: The rule to move, by its code (RU9).

mcp_move_direction.text: up moves it one place earlier, down one place later.

mcp_tool_undo.text: Takes back one of your own changes while it can still be undone. Name the change by the request id you sent with the write that made it: send request with a write you may want to take back. Only a record that keeps revisions (such as an app) keeps what an undo takes back; any other change is refused as having kept nothing to undo. Also refused when the change was not yours, it can no longer be undone, someone changed its record since, it made a new record (delete that instead), or that kind of change cannot be taken back. An older change, or one that kept nothing, is set back with the tool that changed it. Answers the change's own undone words.

mcp_tool_task_run_end.text: Asks a running or paused system task run to stop: it stops once it finishes the item it is working on. A run that already ended is refused. Needs the right to manage system tasks. Answers that the stop was asked; list kind=task_run shows the run's state.

mcp_code_task_run_end.text: The run to stop, by its code (TR7).

mcp_tool_task_run_pause.text: Pauses or resumes a system task run. With paused true, a running run finishes the item it is working on and then waits, keeping its place, until it is resumed; with paused false, a paused run goes on from where it waits. Only a task that declares it can be paused can be; a run that is stopping, already ended, or carried out elsewhere is refused. Needs the right to manage system tasks. Answers that it was paused or resumed.

mcp_code_task_run_pause.text: The run to pause or resume, by its code (TR7).

mcp_task_run_paused.text: true pauses the run, false resumes it.

set_template_variable_description.text: Declares, changes, renames or removes a template's variable, named by its key, as its Contents tab does.

set_template_database_description.text: Declares, changes, renames or removes a template's managed database, named by its variable prefix, as its Contents tab does.

create_game_address_description.text: Routes an address to a game app through a proxy app, through the game address page's own form.

change_game_address_description.text: Changes a game address's address, apps, port or switch through its own form.

create_certificate_description.text: Stores your own certificate with its private key, through the certificate page's upload form.

change_certificate_description.text: Changes a certificate's name, its chain and key where Hohenheim holds the key, or whether it renews by itself.

create_dns_peer_description.text: Adds a nameserver or another Hohenheim to exchange zones with, through the peer page's own form.

change_dns_peer_description.text: Changes a DNS peer's settings through its own form; a secret left out stays as it is.

make_build_hook_description.text: Makes a build hook for an app; its URL waits, shown once, for the account that made it on the app's Build hooks tab.

replace_build_hook_url.text: Give a build hook a new URL
{$actor} gave build hook {$subject} a new URL

replace_build_hook_url_description.text: Replaces a build hook's URL, the old one dead at once; the new one waits, shown once, for the account that asked on the app's Build hooks tab.

set_quota.text: {$actor} set the limits of an owner

set_quota_description.text: Sets, changes or removes the limits of one owner, its people and roles named by their codes, as the limits page does.

sign_certificate.text: Order a certificate from a signing request
{$actor} ordered certificate {$subject} from a signing request

sign_certificate_description.text: Has Let's Encrypt issue a certificate for the caller's own signing request; the private key never reaches Hohenheim.

resign_certificate.text: Re-issue from a new signing request
{$actor} re-issued certificate {$subject} from a new signing request

resign_certificate_description.text: Re-issues a certificate whose key its requester holds from a new signing request, the one way its key changes.

import_dns_zone_description.text: Replaces a primary zone's records with those of pasted zone-file text, as its Zone file tab does.

mcp_tool_template_variable_set.text: Declares, changes or removes one question a template (TP3) asks when an app is made from it, named by template and key. The key becomes the app's variable and the \{\{KEY\}\} token in its command, cloud_init and config files; the type decides what value is accepted, and a setting of another type is refused. new_key renames it; a new type empties the old type's settings for good. Administrators only. Apps already made keep their values. Answers what changed, or that it was removed.

mcp_tool_template_database_set.text: Declares, changes or removes a managed database every app made from a template (TP3) gets, named by template and env_prefix: each new app gets its own database and its connection details as variables named after the prefix (DB gives DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_NAME and DB_URL; an app's first database also DATABASE_URL). new_env_prefix renames it. The template must run on Docker hosts. Administrators only. Apps already made keep their databases, also after a remove.

mcp_code_template_part.text: The template's code (TP3) the declaration belongs to.

mcp_tool_game_address_set.text: Routes an address (D4, exact match) to a game app through a proxy app: the proxy forwards players connecting to that hostname to the backend's port. The backend and the proxy are different apps on the same host, and an address is routed once per proxy. Not an app's own game_hostname, which its kind tool sets. Administrators only. Removing is delete GD1, which also removes the DNS records the mapping made. Answers the mapping's code (GD1).

mcp_code_game_address_set.text: The game address's code (GD1); leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_build_hook_set.text: Makes a build hook for an app (AP12) whose releases Hohenheim manages: a secret URL that deploys the app when anything POSTs to it. With code, the hook (BH4) gets a new URL and the old one stops at once; nothing else of a hook changes. The URL is never in the answer: it waits, shown once to the account behind this call, on the app's Build hooks tab in the panel, for 24 hours. Revoking is delete BH4. Answers the hook's code.

mcp_code_build_hook_set.text: The hook's code (BH4); leave out to make one.

mcp_build_hook_parked.text: build hook {$hook}: its URL waits, shown once to the account behind this call, on the Build hooks tab of {$app} in the panel, for 24 hours

mcp_tool_quota_set.text: Sets the limits of one owner: a person (U4), a role (RO2), or several together for an owner they share, in any order; an empty list is the administrators' own limits. The same owners again changes them; remove takes them away and the installation's defaults apply again. Here a limit of 0 allows nothing new, and null falls back to the installation's default. A limit is checked when something is created, never afterwards, so lowering one removes nothing running. Administrators only. Answers the owners' names.

mcp_tool_certificate_set.text: Uploads your own certificate with its private key, or changes a stored certificate (C8): its listed name, its chain and key where Hohenheim holds the key, or with auto_renew whether a Let's Encrypt certificate renews by itself. The chain must parse and the key must belong to its first certificate. An uploaded certificate is never renewed: upload its successor before it expires; to have one issued, use certificate_order or certificate_sign. A replaced chain and key cannot be brought back. Administrators only. Answers the C code.

mcp_code_certificate_set.text: The certificate's code (C8); leave out to upload one.

mcp_tool_certificate_sign.text: Has Let's Encrypt issue a certificate for your own signing request (a PEM CSR) for exactly hostnames; your private key never reaches Hohenheim, which renews from that request. With code, re-issues such a certificate (C8) from a NEW request, the only way its key changes. Only for names of sites you manage; the challenge is chosen for you (DNS through a zone hosted here when possible, else HTTP, which needs each name to point here). The same key for the same names answers the existing certificate. Answers the C code and whether it was issued.

mcp_code_certificate_sign.text: The certificate (C8) to re-issue from a new signing request; leave out to order a new one.

certificate_signed_thing.text: a certificate from your signing request

mcp_tool_dns_zone_import.text: Replaces a primary zone's records with those of the zone-file text you paste; records Hohenheim made itself (certificate proofs) stay. The file's apex NS records are dropped for the installation's declared nameservers unless keep_ns. $INCLUDE is not read; lines that cannot be imported are skipped and named in the answer. A secondary zone is refused: import on the peer that owns it. Cannot be undone except by importing the old text: read it first with dns_record_list as_zone_text. Administrators only. Answers how many records came in.

mcp_code_dns_zone_import.text: The primary zone (Z7, or its origin such as example.com) whose records are replaced.

mcp_tool_dns_peer_set.text: Creates or changes a DNS peer (DP2): another nameserver this Hohenheim exchanges zones with by zone transfer, or another Hohenheim, which also takes forwarded record edits over its admin API and can keep every zone. A plain nameserver needs transfer_host; a Hohenheim peer base_url and api_key. Secrets go in once and are never shown again. negotiate_key with a peer's code makes a fresh shared transfer key on both sides, so no secret is copied by hand; the key used before stops at once. Administrators only. Answers the DP code, or the key's name.

mcp_code_dns_peer_set.text: The peer's code (DP2); leave out to create one.

mcp_negotiate_key.text: Make a new shared transfer key with this Hohenheim peer and install it on both sides, instead of changing its settings.

template_variable_remove.text: Removes this question from the template; apps already made keep their value.

template_variable_new_key.text: A new key for this question; apps already made keep their variable under the old key.

template_database_new_prefix.text: A new prefix for this declaration; apps already made keep their variables under the old one.

template_database_remove.text: Removes this declaration from the template; apps already made keep their databases.

template_variable_description.text: A longer explanation of what the value is for, shown on the create-app form.

template_variable_required.text: Whether an app cannot be created without a value; a switch is never required and a generated secret never asked for.

variable_min_value.text: The smallest number a create accepts for this variable.

variable_max_value.text: The largest number a create accepts for this variable.

variable_longest.text: The longest value accepted, in characters; 0 or less means no limit.

variable_secret_bytes.text: How many random bytes a generated secret holds; 0 or less means 32.

game_address_enabled.text: Whether the proxy routes this address.

build_hook_app.text: The app (AP12) the hook deploys; it cannot change later.

quota_owners.text: The people (U4) and roles (RO2) that share these limits, by their codes, in any order.

quota_remove.text: Removes this owner's limits; the installation's defaults apply again.

certificate_signing_request.text: Your signing request, one PEM CERTIFICATE REQUEST block naming exactly the hostnames. It is public; the key that signed it stays with you.

dns_zone_text.text: The zone-file text, as another provider exports it; at most 1,048,576 characters.

dns_keep_ns.text: Keep the file's apex NS records instead of writing the nameservers the installation declares.

keyed_change_only.text: {$name} renames one that exists; none is named by these keys yet.

build_hook_no_account.text: A build hook's URL is shown only to the account that made it, and no account stands behind this call.

build_hook_urls_waiting.text: Build hook URLs an assistant made for you, shown only now: {$urls}

mcp_tool_spam_service_set.text: Configures the spam service this Hohenheim runs itself: whether it runs, its port, the host account it runs as and its heap size. Only what you send changes. Saving brings the running service in line in the background: spam_service_test shows whether it answers, spam_service_power starts, stops or restarts it by hand. An enabled service does not start without a host account. Its scoring settings are read with settings_read section=spam. Administrators only. Answers the settings written.

mcp_tool_spam_service_power.text: Starts, stops or restarts the spam service this Hohenheim runs itself; it has no code. Start and restart need it enabled (spam_service_set enabled); stop needs it running and leaves enabled as it is. Stop and restart make the service unavailable meanwhile, and every spam tool is refused until it answers again. The work goes on in the background: spam_service_test shows when it answers. Administrators only. Answers that it was requested.

mcp_spam_service_action.text: Whether to start, stop or restart the service; restart also reloads its configuration.

mcp_tool_spam_service_test.text: Asks the spam service this Hohenheim runs itself for its status now; it has no code. It changes nothing in the service, but writes one activity line per check. Refused while the service is not configured, disabled, not running or not yet connected, each in its own sentence. Administrators only. Answers the status the service reports, or why it did not answer.

mcp_tool_spam_word_set.text: Adds, changes or removes a scored word or phrase of the spam service's dictionary: a submission containing it weighs that many points towards spam. A word is named by itself and its word_language: the same pair again changes it, remove takes it away. Only what you send changes. The spam service must be running. A changed score or a removed word is not kept anywhere. Administrators only. Answers whether the word was added, changed or removed.

mcp_tool_spam_reputation_read.text: Explains an IP address's reputation as this Hohenheim weighs it for automatic bans: the IP intelligence datasets that know it (hosting, VPN, Tor and the like, which never count towards a ban), its negative and positive security-event counts per category, the weighted score per category and the net score against the ban threshold. The spam service must be running. It changes nothing; banning is ban_set. Administrators only.

mcp_tool_notification_channel_set.text: Creates or changes a notification channel (NC2): a webhook (Slack, Discord or generic JSON) this Hohenheim posts its alerts to, and which alerts it gets. A channel with no events gets every event, including ones a later version adds. Every alert also reaches every administrator's inbox. The URL goes in once and is never shown again. Send a test alert with test code=NC2; after delete its alerts silently stop. Administrators only. Answers the code.

mcp_code_notification_channel_set.text: The channel's code (NC2); leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_delivery_retry.text: Sends a failed notification delivery again: it is queued with a fresh attempt budget and tried once at once. Only a delivery that failed for good can be retried; failed ones are listed with list kind=delivery. It needs the right to manage the delivery log. Answers whether this attempt delivered it; when not, the background sweep keeps trying until its attempts run out.

mcp_code_delivery_retry.text: The failed delivery's code (ND3), as list kind=delivery shows it.

mcp_tool_notification_mark_read.text: Marks items of your own notification inbox read: one item (code), every item about one record (about), or every item (neither). It only records that you read them; it changes nothing else, and an item stays in the inbox. Items are listed with list kind=notification_inbox_item. Give at most one of code, about. Answers how many items were marked.

mcp_code_notification_mark_read.text: The one inbox item to mark read (N14).

mcp_notification_mark_read_about.text: Marks read every item of yours about this record, named by its code (AP12).

mcp_tool_site_pause.text: Takes a site's addresses out of the route table (paused true), so visitors get the offline page, or puts them back (paused false); its settings stay as they are. Resuming is refused while another enabled site routes one of its addresses, and the site serving this panel cannot be paused. A site already paused, or already online when resuming, is answered so and stays as it is. Answers what became of the site.

mcp_code_site_pause.text: The site to pause or resume (S20).

mcp_site_paused.text: True takes the site offline; false puts it back online.

mcp_tool_app_install_media_set.text: Puts an ISO from its host in a virtual machine's drive, booted before its root disk, or takes every ISO out (remove true); the ISO files stay on the host. A drive holding an ISO is emptied first with remove true. Administrators only. Answers what became of the app.

mcp_code_app_install_media_set.text: The virtual machine app whose drive to fill or empty (AP12).

mcp_install_media_remove.text: True takes every ISO out of the machine's drives; install_media is then left out.

mcp_tool_app_webhook_set.text: Registers the app's push webhook at the git provider its source is bound to, or brings it up to date, so a push starts a deploy. It needs a provider that registers webhooks and a site address with a working HTTPS certificate; an app without a webhook secret gets one made and stored. Administrators only. Answers whether the webhook was created or brought up to date.

mcp_code_app_webhook_set.text: The app whose push webhook to register (AP12).

mcp_tool_app_deploy_list.text: Lists an app's deploys and the builds that never became one, newest first, one page at a time, each by its code (RL4, BU7) with its status, commit, trigger, start and length; logs reads a code's log. Answers one page; with more than one, which of how many.

mcp_code_app_deploy_list.text: The app whose deploys to list (AP12).

set_spamservice_installation_description.text: Saves the spam service's installation as its form does: whether it runs, its port, its host account and its heap size; a setting left out stays as it is.

set_spamservice_word_description.text: Adds, changes or removes the spam word its text and language name, as the dictionary page writes it; a setting left out stays as it is.

read_spamservice_reputation_description.text: Explains one IP address's reputation as the reputation page does: its datasets, its event counts and its weighted score.

create_notification_channel_description.text: Adds a webhook notification channel through the channels list's own form.

change_notification_channel_description.text: Changes what the call sends of a notification channel through its own form; every other setting stays as it is.

delete_notification_channel_description.text: Deletes a notification channel through the channels list's own delete; its alerts stop silently.

spam_service_host_account.text: The account on Hohenheim's own machine the service runs as, by its code (SU12); list kind=host_account lists them.

spam_service_enabled.text: Whether Hohenheim runs the spam service on its own machine; off stops it.

spam_service_port.text: The local port the spam service listens on.

spam_service_max_heap.text: The most heap memory the spam service's Java process may use.

spam_word_word.text: The word or phrase to score, as found in submitted text.

spam_word_language.text: The language the word counts in, an ISO 639-3 code such as nld; left out, every language. Part of the word's key.

spam_word_score.text: Points the word adds towards spam; negative points pull towards wanted mail. Needed to add a word.

spam_word_leet.text: Also match the word spelled in leetspeak (v14gr4).

spam_word_remove.text: Removes the word in this language.

spam_reputation_ip.text: The IPv4 or IPv6 address whose reputation to explain.

notification_channel_name.text: The name the channel is listed by.

notification_channel_format.text: The payload shape the webhook receives; generic is plain JSON.

notification_channel_url.text: The webhook URL alerts are posted to; Slack and Discord carry their token in it, so it is never shown again.

spam_word_duplicates.text: {$word} is in the dictionary {$count} times for this language; remove the duplicates in the panel first.

spam_word_score_needed.text: To add a spam word, give its score.

read_spamservice_reputation.text: {$actor} read the reputation of an IP address

mcp_tool_spam_client_set.text: Creates or changes a client of the spam service (SPC12): an application allowed to submit content for spam checking, with what it may do and how strict its verdicts are. Only what you send changes. The spam service must be running; while it does not answer, every call is refused. Its keys are spam_key_set. A client made by a provisioner through the service's own API carries an external id and owner that cannot be changed here. Administrators only. Answers the client's code.

mcp_code_spam_client_set.text: The client's code (SPC12); leave out to create one.

mcp_tool_spam_key_set.text: Makes a key for a spam-service client, renames one, or switches one off or back on (SPK4). The spam service must be running. A key not given is generated and never answered: it is shown once to the account that made this call, on the client's Keys tab in the panel, for 24 hours. A key given (to adopt one an application already uses) goes in as a secret. enabled=false refuses its callers at once and enabled=true undoes it. Administrators only. Answers the key's code.

mcp_code_spam_key_set.text: The key's code (SPK4); leave out to create one.

mcp_spam_key_made.text: spam key {$key} of {$client}: its key waits, shown once to the account behind this call, on the Keys tab of {$client} in the panel, for 24 hours

mcp_spam_key_adopted.text: spam key {$key} of {$client}: made with the key you gave

mcp_tool_spam_sample_set.text: Gives a spam-service sample (a submission that was checked, SPS381) your verdict, spam or ham, which confirms it and teaches the learned rule; or, with rescore=true, has the service score it again now with today's rules and words. One call does one of the two. The spam service must be running. A confirmed sample can no longer be rescored, and a sample that keeps no words (a mail) cannot be rescored at all. Administrators only. Answers the verdict or the new score.

mcp_code_spam_sample_set.text: The sample to judge or rescore, by its code (SPS381).

mcp_spam_sample_verdict.text: spam confirms the sample as spam; ham confirms it as wanted content.

mcp_spam_sample_rescore.text: True has the service score the sample again with today's rules and words.

spamservice_client_create_description.text: Creates a client at the spam service, as the clients list's form does.

spamservice_client_change_description.text: Changes what the call sends of a spam client, as its form does; every other setting stays as the service holds it.

make_spamservice_key.text: {$actor} made a spam filter client key

make_spamservice_key_description.text: Makes a key under the spam client its code names; a generated key waits, shown once to the caller's account, on the client's Keys tab.

spamservice_key_change_description.text: Renames a spam key or turns it on or off, as its form saves it; what the call leaves out stays.

spamservice_mark_spam_description.text: Confirms a sample as spam, which teaches the learned rule.

spamservice_mark_ham_description.text: Confirms a sample as wanted content, which teaches the learned rule.

spamservice_rescore_description.text: Has the spam service score a sample again with today's rules and words; a confirmed sample cannot be.

spam_client_name.text: The name the client is listed by.

spam_client_enabled.text: Off refuses every check this client sends.

spam_client_trusted.text: We operate this client, so the IP addresses it relays are truthful; only trusted clients' events feed IP reputation.

spam_client_provisioner.text: Lets this client's keys create and update clients of their own through the service's API.

spam_client_manager.text: Lets this client's keys use the service's management API, which can change every client, word and setting.

spam_client_allowed_languages.text: The ISO 639-3 codes this client expects, comma-separated (nld,eng); detected languages outside them score as forbidden. Empty: every language.

spam_client_spam_threshold.text: Samples of this client scoring strictly above this are flagged spam.

spam_key_name.text: A name for the key, shown in the client's key list.

spam_key_enabled.text: Off revokes the key, so its callers lose access at once; on enables a revoked key again.

spam_key_spam_client.text: The spam client the new key belongs to, by its code (SPC12).

spam_key_no_account.text: A generated spam key is shown only to the account that made it, and no account stands behind this call; give key to adopt one instead.

keys_waiting.text: Spam keys an assistant made for you, shown only now: {$keys}

access_log_range_unset.text: Pick when the range starts and when it ends.

access_log_stopped.text: Read back to {$at :datetime}: older lines in this range were not read. Pick a shorter range to see them.

access_log_stopped_early.text: Older lines in this range were not read. Pick a shorter range to see them.

read_site_access_log_description.text: Reads one page of the site's access log, newest first, filtered by status, path, visitor and time.

mcp_tool_access_log_read.text: Reads one site's access log: the requests its addresses answered, newest first, {$lines :integer} lines a page, each as the log file holds it (the address asked for, the visitor's address, time, request, status, bytes, referrer, user agent, then the milliseconds it took). Narrow it by status class or exact code, by text in the path, by visitor address and by from and to. One read goes through at most {$bound :bytes} of log text and then says how far back it came: give from and to for older lines. Days older than the keeping setting are gone. Only someone who manages the site may read it.

mcp_code_access_log_site.text: The site (S14) whose access log to read.

access_log_status.text: Only lines of this status class; 4xx_5xx is every refused and failed request.

access_log_status_code.text: Only lines answered with this exact status, such as 404.

access_log_path.text: Only lines whose path, with its query, holds this text.

access_log_visitor.text: Only lines of this visitor address; ending it in a dot or a colon reads every address it starts.

access_log_from.text: The earliest moment to read; left out, the read goes back as far as its bound.

access_log_to.text: The latest moment to read; left out, up to now.

access_log_page.text: Which page of {$lines :integer} lines to read, 1 for the newest.

traffic_dropped.text: The traffic counters had no room for them since the last start, so the totals of that time are short. A server this busy needs a look.

settings.hohenheim.traffic.label: Traffic
settings.hohenheim.traffic.help: How long the counted traffic of sites and DNS zones is kept, and how often it is written to disk.
settings.hohenheim.traffic.minute_totals: How many days the totals per minute are kept.
settings.hohenheim.traffic.hour_totals_d: How many days the totals per hour are kept.
settings.hohenheim.traffic.day_totals_mo: How many months the totals per day are kept; a read over months reads them.
settings.hohenheim.traffic.flush_seconds: How often the totals still being counted are written to disk; a crash loses at most this much.

traffic_unwritten.text: Traffic totals cannot be written to disk

read_site_traffic_description.text: Reads the site's counted requests over a span: its totals, one line per step and one top table.

read_server_traffic.text: {$actor} read the traffic of every site

read_server_traffic_description.text: Reads the counted requests of every site at once over a span, the names no site serves among them: the totals, one line per step and one top table.

read_dns_zone_queries_description.text: Reads the zone's counted questions over a span: its totals, one line per step and one top table.

mcp_tool_traffic_read.text: Reads a site's counted requests, or with no site every site's at once (administrators only), over a period ending at until: requests against the period before, bytes sent and received, distinct visitors, answers per status class, the median and slowest 5 percent response time, then each step's requests per status class (a minute for an hour, an hour for a day, a day for a week or a month). top adds one table of {$rows :integer} rows and one holding the rest. Totals per minute are kept 2 days, per hour 31 days, per day 13 months. Only someone who manages a site may read it.

mcp_code_traffic_site.text: The site (S14) whose traffic to read; left out, every site's, for administrators.

mcp_tool_dns_zone_queries_read.text: Reads the questions resolvers asked one of this Hohenheim's DNS zones over a period ending at until: questions against the period before, answers per outcome (2xx answered, 4xx no such name or refused, 5xx failed), distinct resolvers, the median and slowest 5 percent answer time, then one line per step with its questions per outcome. top adds one table of {$rows :integer} rows and one holding the rest. Zone transfers and NOTIFY messages are no questions and are not counted. For administrators only.

mcp_code_dns_zone_queries.text: The zone (Z7, or its origin such as example.com) whose questions to read.

traffic_period.text: The span to read back from until: an hour per minute, a day per hour, a week or a month per day.

traffic_until.text: When the span ends, in office time; left out, now.

traffic_top_site.text: One table beside the totals: pages (ids grouped as :id), refused_pages (answered 4xx), slowest_pages (at least 50 requests), referrers, browsers, statuses or visitors (addresses in full); with no site also sites (ranked by requests and by bytes sent) or unserved_names.

traffic_top_zone.text: One table beside the totals: names asked with their type, missing_names (no such name or refused), resolvers or outcomes.

outside_log_rotation.text: Hohenheim rotates this log by day itself, and {$copy} beside it shows a second rotation: the lines that program copies away never reach a day the Access log tab reads. Remove {$rule} on the machine this Hohenheim runs on.

outside_log_rotation_unnamed.text: Hohenheim rotates this log by day itself, and {$copy} beside it shows a second rotation: the lines that program copies away never reach a day the Access log tab reads. Remove the logrotate rule that names this file on the machine this Hohenheim runs on.

traffic_page_hint.text: The requests every site on this server answered, and the names nobody serves.

traffic_top_every_site.text: This table lists every site at once; leave out site to read it.

dns_class_not_answered.text: No such name, refused or malformed

traffic_empty.text: No requests in this period. Requests show here as soon as the site answers them.

traffic_empty_zone.text: No questions in this period. Questions show here as soon as this server answers them.

table_pages_lead.text: A number or id in a path counts as :id.

table_slowest_pages_lead.text: At least {$least :integer} requests in the period.

table_slowest_pages_empty.text: No page had {$least :integer} requests in this period yet.

table_referrers_lead.text: The site a visitor came from.

table_unserved_names_lead.text: Requests for a hostname no site on this server has. They get the default answer.

table_missing_names_lead.text: A name asked often may be one to add.

table_resolvers_lead.text: Resolvers ask on behalf of visitors, by their address.

read_app_network_description.text: Reads what the app received and sent over a span, one line per step, and what each of its sites answered visitors.

mcp_tool_app_network_read.text: Reads what an app received and sent over a period ending at until, counted from its own network counters, visitors and other services together: the totals against the period before, each step's bytes received and sent (a minute for an hour, an hour for a day, a day for a week or a month), then each of its sites with the requests it answered and the bytes it sent visitors through the proxy. The counters are read every 5 minutes while the app runs. top destinations adds where its outgoing connections went, when an administrator records it. Only someone who manages the app may read it.

mcp_code_app_network_read.text: The app (AP12) whose network use to read.

app_network_chart_lead_minute.text: Per minute, everything the app received and sent, visitors and other services together. Its counters are read every 5 minutes while it runs and every second while someone watches its Metrics tab, so a minute holds what moved since the reading before.

app_network_chart_lead_hour.text: Per hour, everything the app received and sent, visitors and other services together.

app_network_chart_lead_day.text: Per day, everything the app received and sent, visitors and other services together.

app_network_nothing_counted_hint.text: Hohenheim reads the app's network counters every 5 minutes while it runs: what it sends and receives appears here within 5 minutes of its start.

app_network_sites_description.text: What visitors asked of the app's sites through the proxy in this span.

app_network_no_sites.text: No site points at this app

app_network_destinations_lead.text: In this span, by destination, the most sent first. Only the connections the app opens itself count, never a visitor's connection to it.

app_network_destinations_footnote.text: Hohenheim counts bytes and connections in its own firewall and never looks inside what is sent. A destination is named by what Hohenheim knows of this server itself: its apps, databases, proxy and sites; any other destination is its address.

app_network_no_destinations.text: No outgoing connections counted in this span

app_network_no_destinations_hint.text: Hohenheim reads every app's connection counters once a minute. A destination appears here a few minutes after the app first connects to it.

app_network_destinations_off.text: Hohenheim does not record where apps send data

app_network_destinations_off_hint.text: An administrator switches it on in the settings, under Traffic: Record where apps send data.

destination_proxy.text: a site on this server, through its address

traffic_top_app.text: One table beside the totals: destinations, where the app's outgoing connections went, each its address, port and protocol, connections, bytes sent and received and when last seen, the most sent first; its database link and its own containers are internal lines.

traffic_destinations_unkept.text: Where apps send data is not counted on {$host}

traffic_destinations_unread.text: Where apps send data cannot be read on {$host}

traffic_destinations_slow.text: Reading where apps send data is slow on {$host}

The last reading of its firewall counters took {$took :duration style=timing}. It runs once a minute, off every request and deploy; a reading this slow needs a look at how many destinations the apps there talk to.

settings.hohenheim.traffic.record_destin: Count, on every host this Hohenheim runs apps on, where each app's outgoing connections go: address, port, protocol, bytes and connections. Content is never read. A change reaches every host within five minutes.

read_app_destinations.text: Reads each host's firewall counters once a minute and counts where every app's outgoing connections went
